helpers.name: trimmed
helpers.code:
case value do
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  nil -> ""
  other -> to_string(other)
end

helpers.name: positive
helpers.code:
cond do
  is_integer(value) and value > 0 ->
    value

  is_binary(value) ->
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {number, _rest} when number > 0 -> number
      _not_a_number -> fallback
    end

  true ->
    fallback
end

helpers.name: to_page
helpers.code:
cond do
  is_integer(value) and value > 0 -> value
  is_binary(value) -> positive(value, 1)
  true -> 1
end

helpers.name: asked_page
helpers.code:
key = to_string(assigns[:page_param] || "page")

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^key => asked} -> to_page(asked)
  _no_params_or_key -> positive(assigns[:page], 1)
end

helpers.name: page_in_url?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER THE ADDRESS NAMED THE PAGE — `page_param` in `params` — rather than the pager's buttons.
key = to_string(assigns[:page_param] || "page")

match?(%{^key => _asked}, assigns[:params])

helpers.name: from_url
helpers.code:
# A CAPTURED SEGMENT AND A QUERY KEY ARRIVE THE SAME WAY. The runtime merges a page's captures into
# the same map as its query string, so /:lang/docs and /docs?lang= are read by one line — and
# `:lang` may sit in ANY segment of the path, because nothing here looks at position. A key an
# author emptied names nothing, and so reads nothing.
name = trimmed(assigns[key])

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^name => found} when name != "" and is_binary(found) -> trimmed(found)
  _no_params_or_key -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_language
helpers.code:
# THE READER MAY ASK FOR A LANGUAGE, AND THE AUTHOR MAY REFUSE TO LET THEM. `lang_param` is the one
# key the language travels under — read here, written onto every link below — so emptying it both
# stops `?lang=` reaching this block and stops it being written, which is what a page whose language
# is a path segment wants and what a page meant to be in one language only wants.
case from_url(assigns, :lang_param) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:lang])
  asked -> asked
end

helpers.name: doc_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF AN EDITION, built by `site_path/2` for the site the page renders for — in the
# template and in the task a block reads in alike, because `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4`
# hands the task the page's site. Each segment is appended to the base, and a `:lang` in the base —
# in any position, /:lang/docs or /docs/:lang — is filled with the language of the edition being
# linked to, not the one the page is read in, which is the only way a link to an edition in ANOTHER
# language can be built. The address is the one the site's URL mode gives that language:
# /docs/<document> in a first language the site leaves unprefixed, /fa/docs/<document> in Persian. A
# base without the segment carries the language as a query key instead, so nothing appends it twice.
# An edition whose language this site does not publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than
# a link to a 404.
numbered = Enum.with_index(segments)
pattern = Enum.reduce(numbered, to_string(base), fn {_segment, at}, acc -> acc <> "/:segment#{at}" end)

captures =
  numbered
  |> Map.new(fn {segment, at} -> {"segment#{at}", to_string(segment)} end)
  |> Map.put("lang", trimmed(language))

case site_path(pattern, captures) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    in_path? = ":lang" in String.split(to_string(base), "/")

    query =
      case {in_path?, trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
        {false, key, code} when key != "" and code != "" -> Map.put(extra, key, code)
        _carried_by_the_path_or_not_asked_for -> extra
      end

    case URI.encode_query(query) do
      "" -> path
      encoded -> path <> "?" <> encoded
    end
end

helpers.name: document_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A DOCUMENT, OR OF ONE OF ITS PAGES. A document with an Address of its own is read
# there and its pages under it — /product/docs/headless/switch — and that address is one edition's,
# so no `?lang=` is written onto it; any other is read under the base, by its slug.
case document do
  %{path: own} when is_binary(own) and own != "" ->
    doc_href(own, segments, document.language, "", extra)

  _read_by_its_slug ->
    doc_href(base, [document.slug | segments], document.language, lang_param, extra)
end

helpers.name: text_direction
helpers.code:
case trimmed(language) do
  code when code in ~w(fa ar he ur ps ckb dv yi) -> "rtl"
  _left_to_right_or_unknown -> "auto"
end

helpers.name: page_lang
helpers.code:
# A LIST OF EVERY EDITION IS IN NO ONE LANGUAGE, so its root element claims none and each card
# declares its own. Only a list narrowed to one language can speak for the whole block.
case trimmed(language) do
  "" -> nil
  "all" -> nil
  code -> code
end

helpers.name: rows
helpers.code:
case result do
  {:ok, %{results: found}} -> found
  {:ok, found} when is_list(found) -> found
  _unreadable -> []
end

helpers.name: missing!
helpers.code:
# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)
  socket
else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,
    message: "Sorry, the page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved."
end

helpers.name: paged
narrow_language
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

case wanted do
  "all" -> query
  "" -> Ash.Query.filter(query, is_nil(language_group_id) or language_group_id == id)
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: sorted
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

case sort do
  "updated" -> Ash.Query.sort(query, updated_at: :desc)
  "newest" -> Ash.Query.sort(query, inserted_at: :desc)
  _the_order_an_editor_gave_them -> Ash.Query.sort(query, display_order: :asc, name: :asc)
end

helpers.name: documents_query
helpers.code:
# EVERY DOCUMENT THE READER MAY LIST, BEFORE ANY OF THEM IS ORDERED OR CUT TO A PAGE. The count and
# the page of rows are both read from it, so what is counted is what is listed.
require Ash.Query

query =
  MishkaDocument.Workspace
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
  |> narrow_language(asked.language)

case asked.featured_only do
  true -> Ash.Query.filter(query, featured == true)
  false -> query
end

helpers.name: documents_count
helpers.code:
asked
|> documents_query()
|> Ash.count(tenant: site_id())

helpers.name: counted
helpers.code:
# HOW MANY DOCUMENTS, HOW MANY PAGES AND WHICH PAGE, read in step with the page on every visit. It is
# the one cheap read, and the pager, the empty line and the number of skeletons all hang on it, so
# only the rows themselves wait for a task. A page nobody has is a missing page when the address
# named it, and is clamped to the last one there is when the pager's buttons asked for it. The
# answer carries the term it was read for — `listed/3` stores that rather than what was asked, so a
# clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
with {:ok, total} <- documents_count(asked) do
  pages = max(ceil(total / asked.per_page), 1)

  case asked.page > pages and asked.page_in_url do
    true ->
      {:missing, asked}

    false ->
      page = min(asked.page, pages)
      {:ok, %{asked: %{asked | page: page}, total: total, pages: pages}}
  end
end

helpers.name: documents_page
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

asked
|> documents_query()
|> sorted(asked.sort)
|> Ash.Query.select([
  :id,
  :name,
  :slug,
  :path,
  :description,
  :language,
  :language_group_id,
  :featured,
  :display_order,
  :updated_at
])
|> Ash.read(
  tenant: site_id(),
  page: [limit: asked.per_page, offset: (asked.page - 1) * asked.per_page, count: false]
)
|> paged()

helpers.name: editions_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY EDITION OF EVERY DOCUMENT ON THIS PAGE, IN ONE READ. A chip row per card is a read per card
# otherwise, and a page of twenty documents would pay for twenty-one.
require Ash.Query

groups =
  documents
  |> Enum.map(& &1.language_group_id)
  |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
  |> Enum.uniq()

case groups do
  [] ->
    %{}

  wanted ->
    MishkaDocument.Workspace
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(language_group_id in ^wanted)
    |> Ash.Query.sort(language: :asc)
    |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :slug, :path, :language, :language_group_id])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> rows()
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.language_group_id)
end

helpers.name: editions_for
helpers.code:
# AND NO CHIPS UNDER A DOCUMENT WITH ONE EDITION. Every document written here is the master of a
# group holding itself, so a chip row built without this says "en" under every card on a site that
# publishes in one language.
case Map.get(editions, document.language_group_id) do
  nil -> []
  [_the_only_edition] -> []
  found -> found
end

helpers.name: asked
helpers.code:
# EVERYTHING THE READ DEPENDS ON, AS ONE TERM — AND EVERYTHING A ROW IS DRAWN FROM, which is the
# same term for a reason. It is the argument the task is handed — a plain map rather than the
# socket, so nothing of LiveView's is copied into another process — and it is also what says
# whether anything has to be read at all: `update_many/1` runs on every render of the page holding
# this block, and a block that re-read on each of them would restart its own load whenever
# something else on the page moved.
#
# A STREAMED ROW IS RENDERED ONCE AND NEVER AGAIN. LiveView prunes `stream.inserts` after each
# render, so `@streams.documents` is empty on every render that is not a fresh load and the rows
# already on the page are never rebuilt. An attribute the ROWS read — the card they are drawn with,
# the words inside them, the base their links are built from — therefore cannot reach them by
# re-rendering, so it goes in here instead: a change to one re-reads and re-streams. Words OUTSIDE
# the rows (`heading`, `empty_text`, the pager's labels) are free, because those are drawn afresh
# every render.
%{
  visitor: assigns[:current_user],
  language: asked_language(assigns),
  sort: trimmed(assigns[:sort]),
  featured_only: assigns[:featured_only] == true,
  show_languages: assigns[:show_languages] == true,
  per_page: positive(assigns[:per_page], 6),
  prefix: trimmed(assigns[:id]),
  page: asked_page(assigns),
  page_in_url: page_in_url?(assigns),
  card: trimmed(assigns[:card]),
  doc_base: trimmed(assigns[:doc_base]),
  lang_param: trimmed(assigns[:lang_param]),
  show_description: assigns[:show_description] == true,
  read_text: trimmed(assigns[:read_text]),
  featured_text: trimmed(assigns[:featured_text]),
  show_details: assigns[:show_details] == true,
  version_text: trimmed(assigns[:version_text]),
  pages_text: trimmed(assigns[:pages_text]),
  one_page_text: trimmed(assigns[:one_page_text]),
  updated_text: trimmed(assigns[:updated_text])
}

helpers.name: fetch
arrived
helpers.code:
case result do
  {:ok, rows, opts} ->
    socket
    |> Phoenix.Component.assign(:documents, Phoenix.LiveView.AsyncResult.ok(true))
    |> Phoenix.LiveView.stream(:documents, rows, opts)

  {:error, reason} ->

helpers.name: rowed
helpers.code:
# A ROW CARRIES EVERYTHING ITS CARD IS DRAWN FROM, because it is drawn once and in another process
# than the one that read it: its details, and the editions its language chips link to.
prefix =
  case asked.prefix do
    "" -> "doc"
    id -> id <> "-doc"
  end

Enum.map(documents, fn document ->
  %{
    id: prefix <> "-" <> to_string(document.id),
    doc: document,
    details: Map.get(details, document.id),
    editions: (asked.show_languages && editions_for(editions, document)) || []
  }
end)

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.
socket.private[:runtime_cold] == true

helpers.name: inline?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER THE ROWS ARE READ IN STEP WITH THE PAGE. They are on the GET, so a crawler and a reader with
# no JavaScript are served the cards themselves; on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where
# nobody could be handed a task's answer; and on the first connected mount of a visit that began with
# that GET, which draws the cards at once rather than a skeleton in their place. A visit that
# arrived by a live navigation (`live_visit`) and every later read go to a task, except a first read
# of a list with nothing in it, which has no cards to wait for.
cold?(socket) or not Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) or
  (is_nil(before) and (socket.assigns[:live_visit] != true or total == 0))

helpers.name: read_rows
helpers.code:
# A LIST WITH NOTHING IN IT HAS NO ROWS TO READ.
case total do
  0 -> {:ok, [], reset: true}
  _some -> fetch(asked)
end

helpers.name: failed
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT FAILED DRAWS THE ERROR, NEVER A SKELETON THAT STAYS. A task still running for an earlier
# term is stopped, or its answer would arrive after this one and draw rows over it.
socket
|> Phoenix.LiveView.cancel_async(:documents)
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(
  :documents,
  Phoenix.LiveView.AsyncResult.failed(Phoenix.LiveView.AsyncResult.loading(), {:error, reason})
)
|> Phoenix.LiveView.stream(:documents, [], reset: true)

helpers.name: listed
helpers.code:
asked = counts.asked
total = counts.total
left = total - (asked.page - 1) * asked.per_page

socket =
  Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
    asked: asked,
    page: asked.page,
    pages: counts.pages,
    total: total,
    language: asked.language,
    skeletons: max(min(asked.per_page, left), 0)
  )

case inline?(socket, before, total) do
  true ->
    arrived(socket, read_rows(asked, total))

  false ->
    require Phoenix.LiveView

    # IN THE PAGE'S SITE AND LOCALE: `in_caller_locale/1` hands the task both, as
    # `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4` does, so `site_path/2` and `t/1` answer in it what they
    # answer in the template. `reset` is the loading state, not the cards: it is what puts the
    # skeleton back over a page that was already drawn, and the rows reset the stream themselves.
    Phoenix.LiveView.stream_async(
      socket,
      :documents,
      MishkaGervaz.Messages.in_caller_locale(fn -> read_rows(asked, total) end),
      reset: true
    )
end

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case counted(asked) do
      {:ok, counts} -> listed(socket, counts, before)
      {:missing, _asked} -> missing!(socket)
      {:error, reason} -> failed(socket, reason)
    end
end

helpers.name: edition_links
helpers.code:
# THE CHIPS A CARD DRAWS, prepared here because only this block knows where a document lives.
#
# A CHIP ROW SAYS WHAT EXISTS, so an edition this site has no URL for stays in it as a word —
# `doc_href/5` makes none for a language the site does not publish. That is the truth about it: the
# translation was written, this site does not serve it.
Enum.map(editions, fn edition ->
  %{
    language: edition.language,
    selected: edition.id == document.id,
    href: document_href(doc_base, edition, [], lang_param, %{})
  }
end)

helpers.name: details_of
helpers.code:
# WHAT EACH CARD SAYS ABOUT ITS DOCUMENT, keyed by the document's id: the version a reader lands
# on, the pages of it the visitor may read, the languages it is published in and when it last
# changed — the latest of the document, its version and those pages. Two reads for the whole
# page of documents, whatever its size.
versions = current_versions(documents, visitor)
counted = pages_of(Map.values(versions), visitor)

Map.new(documents, fn document ->
  version = Map.get(versions, document.id)
  pages = (version && Map.get(counted, version.id)) || %{count: 0, updated_at: nil}

  {document.id,
   %{
     version: version && version.version_number,
     pages: pages.count,
     languages: languages_of(editions, document),
     updated_at:
       newest([document.updated_at, version && version.published_at, pages.updated_at])
   }}
end)

helpers.name: current_versions
helpers.code:
# THE VERSION EACH DOCUMENT IS READ AT WITHOUT A ?v=: the one an editor marked latest, else the
# newest published — the version its own pages open on.
require Ash.Query

case Enum.map(documents, & &1.id) do
  [] ->
    %{}

  wanted ->
    MishkaDocument.WorkspaceVersion
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_id in ^wanted)
    |> Ash.Query.select([
      :id,
      :workspace_id,
      :version_number,
      :is_latest_for_version,
      :published_at,
      :inserted_at
    ])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> rows()

helpers.name: pages_of
helpers.code:
# HOW MANY PAGES EACH VERSION HOLDS FOR THIS VISITOR, and when the latest of them changed. A group
# with no page of its own is only a heading, so it is not counted.
require Ash.Query

case Enum.map(versions, & &1.id) do
  [] ->
    %{}

  wanted ->
    MishkaDocument.Section
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_version_id in ^wanted)
    |> Ash.Query.select([:workspace_version_id, :group_heading, :group_page])
    |> Ash.Query.load(:last_modified_at)
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> rows()
    |> Enum.reject(&(&1.group_heading == true and &1.group_page != true))
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.workspace_version_id)
    |> Map.new(fn {version_id, pages} ->
      {version_id,
       %{count: length(pages), updated_at: newest(Enum.map(pages, & &1.last_modified_at))}}
    end)
end

case Enum.filter(moments, &match?(%DateTime{}, &1)) do
  [] -> nil
  found -> Enum.max_by(found, &moment/1)
end

helpers.name: moment

  _never -> 0

helpers.name: trimmed
helpers.code:
case value do
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  nil -> ""
  other -> to_string(other)
end

helpers.name: from_url
helpers.code:
# A CAPTURED SEGMENT AND A QUERY KEY ARRIVE THE SAME WAY. The runtime merges a page's captures into
# the same map as its query string, so /docs/:workspace and /docs?workspace= are read by one line —
# and `:lang` may sit in ANY segment of the path, because nothing here looks at position.
name = trimmed(assigns[key])

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^name => found} when name != "" and is_binary(found) -> trimmed(found)
  _no_params_or_key -> ""
end

helpers.name: missing!
helpers.code:
# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)
  socket
else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,
    message: "Sorry, the page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved."
end

helpers.name: asked_workspace
helpers.code:
# THE AUTHOR'S CHOICE WINS OVER THE URL'S. A block pinned to one document is pinned: it sits on a
# page about that document, and a reader appending ?workspace= must not turn it into another.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> from_url(assigns, :workspace_param)
  pinned -> pinned
end

helpers.name: asked_path
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS THIS PAGE SERVES A DOCUMENT AT, when it is that document's own — /product/docs. A
# block pinned to a document by its slug is the author's choice for a page of their own, and keeps
# it.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:path])
  _pinned -> ""
end

helpers.name: page_subject?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER THIS COMPONENT IS WHAT THE PAGE IS ABOUT, or a block an author placed on a page about
# something else. Only the first decides the response: a document named by the URL, or by the
# address the page serves it at, is the page's own subject, while one PINNED through the
# `workspace` attribute — see `asked_workspace/1` — sits on a page that stands on its own and must
# keep standing.
trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) == "" and
  (trimmed(assigns[:path]) != "" or from_url(assigns, :workspace_param) != "")

helpers.name: asked_language
helpers.code:
# HERE THE URL WINS, which is the opposite of every other key and is the point of a language: a page
# offered in four of them is one page, and the reader says which. `lang_param` is the one key the
# language travels under — read here, written onto every link below — so emptying it stops both, and
# that is how an author pins a page to one language, and how a page whose language is a path segment
# keeps the language out of its query strings.
case from_url(assigns, :lang_param) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:lang])
  asked -> asked
end

helpers.name: doc_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF AN EDITION, built by `site_path/2` for the site the page renders for — in the
# template and in the task a block reads in alike, because `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4`
# hands the task the page's site. Each segment is appended to the base, and a `:lang` in the base —
# in any position, /:lang/docs or /docs/:lang — is filled with the language of the edition being
# linked to, not the one the page is read in, which is the only way a link to an edition in ANOTHER
# language can be built. The address is the one the site's URL mode gives that language:
# /docs/<document> in a first language the site leaves unprefixed, /fa/docs/<document> in Persian. A
# base without the segment carries the language as a query key instead, so nothing appends it twice.
# An edition whose language this site does not publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than
# a link to a 404.
numbered = Enum.with_index(segments)
pattern = Enum.reduce(numbered, to_string(base), fn {_segment, at}, acc -> acc <> "/:segment#{at}" end)

captures =
  numbered
  |> Map.new(fn {segment, at} -> {"segment#{at}", to_string(segment)} end)
  |> Map.put("lang", trimmed(language))

case site_path(pattern, captures) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    in_path? = ":lang" in String.split(to_string(base), "/")

    query =
      case {in_path?, trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
        {false, key, code} when key != "" and code != "" -> Map.put(extra, key, code)
        _carried_by_the_path_or_not_asked_for -> extra
      end

    case URI.encode_query(query) do
      "" -> path
      encoded -> path <> "?" <> encoded
    end
end

helpers.name: document_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A DOCUMENT, OR OF ONE OF ITS PAGES. A document with an Address of its own is read
# there and its pages under it — /product/docs/headless/switch — and that address is one edition's,
# so no `?lang=` is written onto it; any other is read under the base, by its slug.
case document do
  %{path: own} when is_binary(own) and own != "" ->
    doc_href(own, segments, document.language, "", extra)

  _read_by_its_slug ->
    doc_href(base, [document.slug | segments], document.language, lang_param, extra)
end

helpers.name: page_links
helpers.args: pages, sections, base, document, lang_param, extra
helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE OF `document` WITH ITS ADDRESS, or `nil` where it has none — a document in a language
# this site does not publish (`doc_href/5`), or a group with no page of its own, which is only a
# heading — so the template draws that page as a word rather than as a link to nothing. A page's
# address holds the pages it is filed under (`section_paths/1`).
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.map(pages, fn page ->
  case page.group_heading == true and page.group_page != true do
    true ->
      {page, nil}

    false ->
      {page, document_href(base, document, Map.get(paths, page.id, [page.slug]), lang_param, extra)}
  end
end)

helpers.name: only_language
helpers.code:
# A PAGE WRITTEN IN ONE LANGUAGE SERVES THAT LANGUAGE'S EDITION AND NO OTHER. A slug names one
# document per site whatever language it is written in, so without this /fa/docs/<english-slug>
# answers the English document inside a Persian, right-to-left page, with nothing saying the URL was
# wrong. Left empty the block sits on a page that does not address languages at all, and the slug
# decides on its own.
require Ash.Query

case wanted do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: workspace_row
helpers.code:
# A DOCUMENT IS FOUND BY THE ADDRESS ITS OWN PAGES SERVE IT AT — `path` — and by its slug
# everywhere else. A slug the URL names finds only a document with no address of its own: one that
# has an address is read there and nowhere else, so /docs/<its slug> is a missing page. A slug the
# author PINNED — see `asked_workspace/1` — finds the document wherever it is read.
require Ash.Query

wanted =
  case {trimmed(path), trimmed(slug)} do
    {"", ""} -> nil
    {"", by_slug} when pinned -> {:pinned, by_slug}
    {"", by_slug} -> {:slug, by_slug}
    {address, _slug} -> {:path, address}
  end

case wanted do
  nil ->
    nil

  {by, value} ->
    # AS THE SYSTEM, since a page whose own lock opens is drawn inside a document that does not.
    query =
      MishkaDocument.Workspace
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
      |> only_language(language)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name, :slug, :path, :description, :language, :updated_at])

    case by do
      :pinned -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value)
      :slug -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value and is_nil(path))
      :path -> Ash.Query.filter(query, path == ^value)
    end
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
    |> first_row()
end

helpers.name: versions_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY VERSION A READER MAY BE SENT TO, resolved through the public read rather than by id. That is
# what keeps a draft version out: `?v=` names a NUMBER, and a number that is not in this list is not
# a version this document publishes, whoever typed it.
# AS THE SYSTEM, as `workspace_row/2` reads the document.
require Ash.Query

case workspace do
  nil ->
    []

  %{id: id} ->
    MishkaDocument.WorkspaceVersion
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
    |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_id == ^id)
    |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :version_number, :is_latest_for_version, :published_at, :inserted_at])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> rows()
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{moment(&1.published_at), moment(&1.inserted_at), &1.id}, :desc)
end

helpers.code:
# VERSION NUMBERS ARE TEXT, so "0.0.10" sorts under "0.0.9" and the newest is whichever one an

  found -> found

helpers.name: sections_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY APPROVED PAGE OF THE VERSION, unpaged: the trail above a page, the pages either side of it
# and the document's own front page are all read off this one list, and a list that stopped at the
# twentieth would give a document of thirty pages a front page missing ten of them.
require Ash.Query

case version do
  nil ->
    []

  %{id: id} ->
    MishkaDocument.Section
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(
      :public_list_at_workspace_version,
      %{workspace_version_id: id},
      read_as(visitor)
    )
    |> Ash.Query.select([
      :id,
      :title,
      :slug,
      :order_position,
      :parent_section_id,
      :front_page,
      :group_heading,
      :group_page
    ])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> rows()
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.order_position || 0, &1.title, &1.id})
end

helpers.name: section_body
helpers.code:
# THE ONE PAGE'S OWN TEXT, read separately so that a document of thirty pages does not run the
# `rendered_content` plugin seam thirty times to draw one of them. `found` is the page as the list
# of the version's pages holds it.
#
# WHEN IT LAST CHANGED IS READ FOR A PAGE THAT SAYS IT. The document's own front page is dated by
# the document (`updated_at/2`), so the two aggregates `last_modified_at` runs over a page's notes
# are left out of its read.
require Ash.Query

loads =
  case found do
    %{front_page: false} -> [:rendered_content, :last_modified_at]
    _front_page -> [:rendered_content]
  end

MishkaDocument.Section
|> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
|> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^found.id)
|> Ash.Query.load(loads)
|> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
|> first_row()

helpers.name: notes_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY APPROVED NOTE, unpaged, because each one is an anchor a table of contents links to and a
# list that stopped short would leave those links pointing at nothing. THE TEXT OF A NOTE IS READ
# WHEN THE NOTES ARE DRAWN (`shown?`): the anchors are made of the titles alone, and a block that
# draws no notes would otherwise carry every note's text for nothing.
require Ash.Query

case section do
  nil ->
    []

  %{id: id} ->
    MishkaDocument.Note
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(section_id == ^id)
    |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :title, :order_position] ++ ((shown? && [:content]) || []))
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> rows()
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.order_position || 0, &1.id})
end

helpers.name: clean
helpers.code:
# STORED MARKUP IS SCRUBBED AGAIN ON THE WAY OUT. It arrives sanitized, but `rendered_content` is a
# plugin seam — anything a site installed may have rewritten it since — and this is the last place
# before a visitor's browser. The scrub is the one a page's text is stored through, which keeps
# classes: a code block's `language-` and the token classes it was highlighted with when it was
# written reach the page as they were stored.
#
# THE LINKS TO OTHER PAGES OF THIS SITE ARE MADE TO NAVIGATE WITH LIVEVIEW IN THE SAME PASS. Each
# is written with the two attributes `<.link navigate>` writes, `data-phx-link="redirect"` and
# `data-phx-link-state="push"`, so a click changes the page in place instead of loading a new one;
# `live_target/2` says which links these are. They are put on what the scrub kept, between its
# traversal and the writing of the markup, so nothing can take them off and the text is read once.
# They are never stored: every page already written draws them with nothing changed. `links` is
# `%{current: the address of the page read, host: the host of this site}`.
#
# THE STEPS ARE `HtmlSanitizeEx.html5/1`'s OWN, one by one: the HTML5 scrubber's `before_scrub/1`,
# the parser, the traversal with that scrubber, the parser's writer. With no link to change the
# result is what `HtmlSanitizeEx.html5/1` returns.
case is_binary(content) do
  true ->
    {tree, _changed} =
      content
      |> HtmlSanitizeEx.Scrubber.HTML5.before_scrub()
      |> HtmlSanitizeEx.Parser.parse()
      |> HtmlSanitizeEx.Traverser.traverse(HtmlSanitizeEx.Scrubber.HTML5)
      |> live_nodes(links)

    HtmlSanitizeEx.Parser.to_html(tree)

  false ->
    ""
end

helpers.name: live_nodes
helpers.code:
# THE SCRUBBED TEXT WITH EACH LINK THAT LEADS TO A PAGE OF THIS SITE WRITTEN LIVE (`live_attrs/2`),
# and how many were changed. A node is a tag with its attributes and its children, a text or a
# comment; a list of nodes is the top of the text.
case node do
  nodes when is_list(nodes) ->
    {live, counts} = nodes |> Enum.map(&live_nodes(&1, links)) |> Enum.unzip()
    {live, Enum.sum(counts)}

  {tag, attrs, children} when is_binary(tag) and is_list(children) ->
    {children, inside} = live_nodes(children, links)

    case tag == "a" && live_attrs(attrs, links) do
      changed when is_list(changed) -> {{tag, changed, children}, inside + 1}
      _stays -> {{tag, attrs, children}, inside}
    end

  other ->
    {other, 0}
end

helpers.name: live_attrs
helpers.code:
# THE ATTRIBUTES OF A LINK ONCE IT IS LIVE, or `nil` when it stays as it is: it may not be live at
# all (`live_anchor?/1`) or its `href` does not lead to a page of this site (`live_target/2`). Every
# attribute it had is kept, in its place, with the two that make it live after them.
with {"href", href} <- List.keyfind(attrs, "href", 0),
     true <- live_anchor?(attrs),
     {:ok, written} <- live_target(href, links) do
  attrs
  |> Enum.map(fn
    {"href", _href} -> {"href", written}
    other -> other
  end)
  |> Kernel.++([{"data-phx-link", "redirect"}, {"data-phx-link-state", "push"}])
else
  _stays -> nil
end

helpers.name: live_anchor?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER A LINK MAY BE MADE LIVE, whatever its `href` says. Not one that opens a window of its own
# (`target`, but `_self`), downloads, says it leads off the site (`rel="external"`), or is a live
# link already.
Enum.all?(attrs, fn
  {"download", _value} -> false
  {"data-phx-link" <> _rest, _value} -> false
  {"target", target} -> String.downcase(target) in ["", "_self"]
  {"rel", rel} -> "external" not in String.split(String.downcase(rel))
  _other -> true
end)

helpers.name: live_target
helpers.code:
# WHERE A LINK LEADS, when that is a page of this site: `{:ok, address}` with the address to write,
# else `:error` and the link stays as it is. The address is read the way the router reads it, with
# its dot segments and percent-encoding resolved, so `/docs/../admin` is the admin. Not a file or a
# route that answers something other than a page (`live_page?/1`), and not the page being read with
# only a fragment to say where in it (`live_here?/2`), which the browser scrolls to and a
# navigation would draw again.
with written when is_binary(written) <- live_written(href, links.host),
     address when is_binary(address) <-
       :uri_string.normalize(URI.encode(written, &(URI.char_unescaped?(&1) or &1 == ?%))),
     %URI{path: path} = target <- URI.parse(address),
     true <- live_page?(String.split(path, "/", trim: true)),
     false <- live_here?(target, links.current) do
  {:ok, written}
else
  _stays -> :error
end

helpers.name: live_written
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS A LINK IS WRITTEN WITH, or `nil` when it is not one of this site's. A path from the
# site's root is, as it is: `/docs/install`, never `//elsewhere`, `docs/install`, `#top` or
# `?page=2`. So is an address in full on the host of this site, `host`, written as the path it is,
# because the page is on that host already, whatever the scheme or the port of the link. A character
# a browser would read differently from the way it is written, a backslash, a space or a control
# character, leaves it a plain link, and so does a path that would begin `//`.
cond do
  Enum.any?(:binary.bin_to_list(href), &(&1 <= 0x20 or &1 == 0x7F or &1 == ?\\)) ->
    nil

  String.starts_with?(href, "/") ->
    (not String.starts_with?(href, "//") && href) || nil

  is_binary(host) and String.starts_with?(href, ["http://", "https://"]) ->
    uri = URI.parse(href)
    path = (uri.path in [nil, ""] && "/") || uri.path

    cond do
      uri.userinfo != nil or uri.port not in [80, 443] ->
        nil

      String.downcase(uri.host || "") != String.downcase(host) ->
        nil

      String.starts_with?(path, "//") ->
        nil

      true ->
        URI.to_string(%URI{path: path, query: uri.query, fragment: uri.fragment})
    end

  true ->
    nil
end

helpers.name: live_here?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER A LINK LEADS TO THE PAGE BEING READ, `current`, with a fragment to say where in it: the
# same path and the same query. A link to the page with no fragment is a link to draw the page
# again, and `current` is `nil` where the page has no address of its own.
case {target.fragment, current} do
  {fragment, current} when is_binary(fragment) and is_binary(current) ->
    here = URI.parse(current)

    String.trim_trailing(target.path, "/") == String.trim_trailing(here.path || "", "/") and
      (target.query || "") == (here.query || "")

  _no_fragment_or_no_address ->
    false
end

helpers.name: live_page?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER A PATH, as its segments, IS A PAGE OF THIS SITE rather than a file or a route that answers
# something other than a page: the admin, the API, the files the site serves (`uploads`, `assets`,
# `fonts`, `images`), the sitemaps, the feeds and the webhooks, the installer, the queue's
# dashboard, GraphQL and the previews. A last segment with an extension is a file, `.pdf` or `.xml`
# or `.gz`; a number after a dot, as in the version of a page, `/docs/1.2.0`, is not one.
reserved =
  ~w(_preview admin api assets feed feeds fonts gql images install oban uploads webhooks)

case segments do
  [] ->
    true

  [first | _rest] ->
    first = String.downcase(first)

    extension =
      segments
      |> List.last()
      |> Path.extname()
      |> String.trim_leading(".")
      |> String.to_charlist()

    letter? = &(&1 in ?a..?z or &1 in ?A..?Z)

    file? =
      extension != [] and length(extension) <= 10 and
        Enum.all?(extension, &(letter?.(&1) or &1 in ?0..?9)) and Enum.any?(extension, letter?)

    not (first in reserved or String.starts_with?(first, "sitemap") or file?)
end

helpers.name: site_host
helpers.code:
# THE HOST THIS SITE ANSWERS ON, which is how a link written out in full to one of its own pages is
# told from one to another site (`live_written/2`). `nil` when the site is not known, and then only
# a path from the site's root is a link to one of its pages.
case MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.States.SiteState.get(site_id()) do
  {:ok, %{host: host}} when is_binary(host) -> host
  _unknown -> nil
end

helpers.name: with_version
helpers.code:
# EVERY `{{doc.version}}` OF A PAGE'S TEXT — `{{ doc.version }}` too — IS `number`, the version the
# reader is reading, HTML-escaped: in its code blocks and in a marker's attributes as well, so an
# install line or a link to a release follows the version picked. `\{{doc.version}}` is drawn as
# `{{doc.version}}`. With no number, the text is handed back as it is. `doc-section`, `doc-toc` and
# `doc-section-cards` carry this word for word, and
# `MishkaDocumentWeb.Live.ExamplePreview.with_version/2` is the same rule.
case is_binary(html) and is_binary(number) and String.contains?(html, "{{") do
  false ->
    html

  true ->
    filled = number |> Phoenix.HTML.html_escape() |> Phoenix.HTML.safe_to_string()

    Regex.replace(~r/(\\?)\{\{\s*doc\.version\s*\}\}/u, html, fn whole, escape ->
      case escape do
        "" -> filled
        _escaped -> String.slice(whole, 1..-1//1)
      end
    end)
end

helpers.name: strip_tags
helpers.code:
value
|> to_string()
|> String.replace(~r/<[^>]*>/, " ")
|> String.replace(" ", " ")
|> String.replace("<", "<")
|> String.replace(">", ">")
|> String.replace(""", "\"")
|> String.replace("'", "'")
|> String.replace("&", "&")
|> String.replace(~r/\s+/u, " ")
|> String.trim()

helpers.name: anchor_slug
helpers.code:
# A TITLE'S OWN WORDS, IN ANY ALPHABET: lower case, every run of what is not a letter or a digit
# one `-`, none at either end, and `""` when nothing is left. `[^a-z0-9]` would empty a Persian or
# Arabic title, so letters and digits are matched by their Unicode category. `doc-section` and
# `doc-toc` carry this, `anchors_of/3`, `free_anchor/3` and `note_anchors/1` word for word, so a
# heading and a note are named by one rule in both.
text
|> to_string()
|> String.downcase()
|> String.replace(~r/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u, "-")
|> String.trim("-")

helpers.name: anchors_of
helpers.code:
# ONE ANCHOR PER TITLE, IN THE ORDER GIVEN: its slug (`anchor_slug/1`), or `<fallback>-<place>`
# counted from 1 when it has none, and never one in `taken` or minted before it — the second of a
# slug is `-2`, the third `-3` (`free_anchor/3`).
texts
|> Enum.with_index(1)
|> Enum.map_reduce(MapSet.new(taken), fn {text, place}, used ->
  base =
    case anchor_slug(text) do
      "" -> fallback <> "-" <> Integer.to_string(place)
      slug -> slug
    end

  anchor = free_anchor(base, used, 1)
  {anchor, MapSet.put(used, anchor)}
end)
|> elem(0)

helpers.name: free_anchor
helpers.code:
# `base` when no anchor in `used` is, else the first of `base-2`, `base-3`, … that is free.
candidate =
  case tried do
    1 -> base
    _later -> base <> "-" <> Integer.to_string(tried)
  end

case MapSet.member?(used, candidate) do
  true -> free_anchor(base, used, tried + 1)
  false -> candidate
end

helpers.name: note_anchors
helpers.code:
# THE ANCHOR OF EACH NOTE OF THE PAGE, BY ITS ID: the slug of its title, `#color-palette`, or
# `note-<place>` for a title with no letter or digit. `notes` are in the order the page draws
# them, which is the order the second note of one title is told apart in.
notes
|> Enum.map(& &1.id)
|> Enum.zip(anchors_of(Enum.map(notes, & &1.title), "note", []))
|> Map.new()

helpers.name: heading_entries
helpers.code:
# THE HEADINGS OF A PAGE, AND THE ID EACH ONE ANSWERS TO, minted by `anchors_of/3` clear of `taken`,
# the anchors the page's notes answer to. `doc-toc` runs exactly this over exactly the same scrubbed
# markup and the same notes, so the two agree on every anchor.
entries =
  ~r/<(h[23])(?:\s[^>]*)?>(.*?)<\/\1>/su
  |> Regex.scan(html)
  |> Enum.map(fn [_whole, tag, inner] -> %{text: strip_tags(inner), level: tag} end)

entries
|> Enum.map(& &1.text)
|> anchors_of("heading", taken)
|> Enum.zip_with(entries, fn id, entry -> Map.put(entry, :id, id) end)

helpers.name: with_heading_ids
helpers.code:
# THE SAME IDS, WRITTEN ONTO THE MARKUP. They are minted here, after the scrub, and an id an author
# wrote onto a heading is dropped for the one minted, so every heading answers the anchor `doc-toc`
# lists and no page carries the same id twice.
ids = Enum.map(heading_entries(html, taken), & &1.id)

~r/<(h[23])(?:\s[^>]*)?>.*?<\/\1>/su
|> Regex.split(html, include_captures: true)
|> Enum.map_reduce(0, fn part, index ->
  case Regex.run(~r/^<(h[23])((?:\s[^>]*)?)>(.*)<\/h[23]>$/su, part) do
    [_whole, tag, attrs, inner] ->
      id = Enum.at(ids, index, "heading-" <> to_string(index + 1))
      kept = String.replace(attrs, ~r/\sid=("[^"]*"|'[^']*')/, "")

      {"<#{tag}#{kept} id=\"#{id}\">#{inner}</#{tag}>", index + 1}

    _not_a_heading ->
      {part, index}
  end
end)
|> elem(0)
|> Enum.join()

helpers.name: climb
helpers.code:
# THE TRAIL UP TO A PAGE, walked over the pages already in hand rather than through the resource's
# own ancestor query, which an unauthenticated reader may not run. Twenty steps is the ceiling: a
# parent chain that loops is a bug in somebody's data and must cost twenty comparisons, not a
# visitor's page.
case {node, length(gathered)} do
  {nil, _nowhere} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, depth} when depth >= 20 ->
    gathered

  {%{parent_section_id: nil}, _at_the_top} ->
    gathered

  {%{parent_section_id: parent}, _keep_going} ->
    case Enum.find(sections, &(&1.id == parent)) do
      nil -> gathered
      found -> climb(sections, found, [found | gathered])
    end
end

helpers.name: crumbs_to
helpers.code:
case section do
  nil -> []
  %{id: id} -> climb(sections, Enum.find(sections, &(&1.id == id)), [])
end

helpers.name: neighbours
rooted?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER WALKING UP FROM A PAGE EVER REACHES THE TOP. A pair of pages filed under each other is
# reachable from neither end, so without this both of them would be missing from the document's
# front page with nothing saying why. Twenty steps is deeper than any manual and cheap.
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _gone} ->
    true

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    false

  {%{parent_section_id: nil}, _at_the_top} ->
    true

  {%{parent_section_id: parent}, _keep_going} ->
    case Map.get(by_id, parent) do
      nil -> true
      found -> rooted?(by_id, found, depth + 1)
    end
end

helpers.name: effective_parent
helpers.code:
# THE PARENT A PAGE IS DRAWN UNDER, which is not always the parent it names. A parent still waiting
# on a review is not published, and hanging its children off it would drop them out of the document
# altogether — so they surface at the top instead, and so does anything in a loop. `doc-sidebar`
# decides the same question the same way, so the front page, the pager and the contents agree.
parent = section.parent_section_id

cond do
  is_nil(parent) -> nil
  not Map.has_key?(by_id, parent) -> nil
  not rooted?(by_id, section, 0) -> nil
  true -> parent
end

helpers.name: roots
helpers.code:
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})

Enum.filter(sections, &(effective_parent(by_id, &1) == nil))

helpers.name: landing_pages
helpers.code:
# THE PAGES AT THE TOP OF THE DOCUMENT, each a link, the groups among them drawn apart as
# headings over their own (`landing_groups/1`).
Enum.reject(roots(sections), &(&1.group_heading == true))

helpers.name: landing_groups
helpers.code: Enum.filter(roots(sections), &(&1.group_heading == true))

helpers.name: group_pages
helpers.code:
# THE PAGES A GROUP HOLDS, in the order the contents draw them, a group inside it giving up its own
# pages in its place: a heading under a heading has no page of its own to list.
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})

sections
|> Enum.group_by(&effective_parent(by_id, &1))
|> grouped_pages(group.id, 0)

helpers.name: grouped_pages
helpers.code:
case depth >= 20 do
  true ->
    []

  false ->
    by_parent
    |> Map.get(parent_id, [])
    |> Enum.flat_map(fn
      %{group_heading: true} = inner -> grouped_pages(by_parent, inner.id, depth + 1)
      page -> [page]
    end)
end

helpers.name: descend
helpers.code:
case depth >= 20 do
  true ->
    []

  false ->
    by_parent
    |> Map.get(parent_id, [])
    |> Enum.flat_map(&[&1 | descend(by_parent, &1.id, depth + 1)])
end

helpers.name: reading_order
helpers.code:
# THE ORDER A READER GOES THROUGH A DOCUMENT IN — a page, then the pages filed under it, then the
# next page beside it, which is the order `doc-sidebar` draws them in. Taking the flat list instead
# puts a child of the first chapter between two chapters, because a page's position is counted among
# its siblings and not among its uncles, and Next then leaves the chapter the reader is in. A group
# is no stop on the way, unless it has a page of its own to read.
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})

sections
|> Enum.group_by(&effective_parent(by_id, &1))
|> descend(nil, 0)
|> Enum.reject(&(&1.group_heading == true and &1.group_page != true))

helpers.name: section_paths
helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE'S OWN PART OF ITS ADDRESS — the slugs of the pages it is drawn under, then its own:
# headless/switch. The parents are the ones `effective_parent/2` draws it under, so a page's address
# is where the reader finds it in the contents. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent,
# so the same one under two parents is two addresses. The front page's is empty (`path_up/4`).
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})
Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, path_up(by_id, &1, [], 0)})

helpers.name: path_up
helpers.code:
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _at_the_top} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    gathered

  # A FRONT PAGE'S SLUG IS NO PART OF ANY ADDRESS. It is drawn at the document's own address, and the
  # pages filed under it sit directly under that.
  {%{front_page: true} = front, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, front)), gathered, depth + 1)

  # A GROUP WITH A PAGE OF ITS OWN IS READ AT ITS SLUG: the first step is the page being addressed,
  # and the group's own page is addressed by its slug.
  {%{group_heading: true, group_page: true} = group, 0} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), [group.slug | gathered], 1)

  # NOR A GROUP'S, above the page addressed: it is a heading, and the pages under it are addressed as
  # if it were not there.
  {%{group_heading: true} = group, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), gathered, depth + 1)

  {page, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, page)), [page.slug | gathered], depth + 1)
end

helpers.name: section_at_path
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE AN ADDRESS NAMES: the one whose own part of the address is exactly the one asked —
# headless/switch. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent, not in the document, so
# `switch` alone may be two pages. Nothing asked is the document's own address, which is the
# version's front page when it has one: the one page whose own part of the address is empty. A group
# is the page at an address only when it has a page of its own (`group_page`).
asked = String.split(trimmed(wanted), "/", trim: true)
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.find(
  sections,
  &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and Map.get(paths, &1.id) == asked)
)

helpers.name: note_blocks
helpers.args: notes, anchors, labels, id, placement, number, links
helpers.code:
# EACH NOTE WITH THE ANCHOR IT IS DRAWN AT, from `anchors` (`note_anchors/1`): `#color-palette`,
# which `doc-toc` links to.
Enum.map(notes, fn note ->
  anchor = Map.fetch!(anchors, note.id)

  %{
    id: note.id,
    anchor: anchor,
    title: note.title,
    html: code_windows(
      placed_cards(
        with_version(example_sources(clean(note.content, links), "note/#{note.id}"), number),
        placement
      ),
      labels,
      "#{id}-#{anchor}"
    )
  }
end)

helpers.name: placement
helpers.code:
# WHAT A `doc-section-cards` PLACED IN THIS PAGE IS TOLD, as the attributes of its marker: the page
# it is in (`placed_in`), and the base, the language key and the version key this block links with,
# so its cards link as this block does. `nil` when no page is read.
case section do
  nil ->
    nil

  %{id: id} ->
    [
      placed_in: id,
      doc_base: assigns[:doc_base],
      lang_param: assigns[:lang_param],
      version_param: assigns[:version_param]
    ]
    |> Enum.map_join(fn {key, value} ->
      ~s( #{key}="#{String.replace(trimmed(value), ["\"", "]", "\\"], "")}")
    end)
end

helpers.name: placed_cards
helpers.code:
# EVERY `doc-section-cards` MARKER IN THE TEXT, HANDED `placement` (`placement/2`) right after its
# name, so the block lists the pages under the page it is drawn in. Only a marker in the text: one
# inside `<pre>` or `<code>` is a page showing the syntax, and is left as it was written.
case is_binary(placement) and String.contains?(html, "doc-section-cards") do
  false ->
    html

  true ->
    marker = ~r/\[\[component((?:\s| | |\x{00A0})+)doc-section-cards(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])/u

    ~r/<(pre|code)(?:\s[^>]*)?>.*?<\/\1>/s
    |> Regex.split(html, include_captures: true)
    |> Enum.map_join(fn part ->
      case Regex.match?(~r/\A<(?:pre|code)[\s>]/, part) do
        true ->
          part

        false ->
          Regex.replace(marker, part, fn _whole, space ->
            "[[component" <> space <> "doc-section-cards" <> placement
          end)
      end
    end)
end

helpers.name: example_sources
helpers.code:
# EVERY `doc-example` MARKER IN THE TEXT, HANDED `source="<source>/<n>"` right after its name, `n`
# counting them from 0 in the order they are written, those inside other markers too: the example's
# preview is the page `/_preview/doc-example/<source>/<n>`, which finds it by this same count
# (`MishkaDocumentWeb.Live.ExamplePreview.sources/2`). Only a marker in the text: one inside `<pre>`
# or `<code>` is a page showing the syntax, and is left as it was written.
case String.contains?(html, "doc-example") do
  false ->
    html

  true ->
    marker = ~r/\[\[component(?:\s| | |\x{00A0})+doc-example(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])/u
    whole = ~r/\A\[\[component(?:\s| | |\x{00A0})+doc-example\z/u

    ~r/<(pre|code)(?:\s[^>]*)?>.*?<\/\1>/s
    |> Regex.split(html, include_captures: true)
    |> Enum.map_reduce(0, fn part, at ->
      case Regex.match?(~r/\A<(?:pre|code)[\s>]/, part) do
        true ->
          {part, at}

        false ->
          {pieces, next} =
            marker
            |> Regex.split(part, include_captures: true)
            |> Enum.map_reduce(at, fn piece, n ->
              case Regex.match?(whole, piece) do
                true -> {piece <> ~s( source="#{source}/#{n}"), n + 1}
                false -> {piece, n}
              end
            end)

          {Enum.join(pieces), next}
      end
    end)
    |> elem(0)
    |> Enum.join()
end

helpers.name: code_windows
helpers.code:
# EVERY CODE BLOCK OF A PAGE'S TEXT IN ITS WINDOW (`code_window/3`), each named `<prefix>-code-<n>`
# in the order it comes. Drawn on the way out, after the scrub, and never stored: the page keeps
# only its code, and the button is this block's to draw. Text with no code block is handed back as
# it is.
case String.contains?(html, "<pre") do
  false ->
    html

  true ->
    ~r/<pre(?:\s[^>]*)?>.*?<\/pre>/s
    |> Regex.split(html, include_captures: true)
    |> Enum.map_reduce(0, fn part, at ->
      case Regex.match?(~r/\A<pre(?:\s[^>]*)?>.*<\/pre>\z/s, part) do
        true -> {code_window(part, labels, "#{prefix}-code-#{at}"), at + 1}
        false -> {part, at}
      end
    end)
    |> elem(0)
    |> Enum.join()
end

helpers.name: code_window
helpers.code:
# ONE CODE BLOCK AS THE WINDOW IT IS READ IN: a head holding its language and a button that copies # its code, over the block exactly as it was stored. Each element says what it is in its # `data-role` — `doc-code`, `doc-code-head`, `doc-code-lang`, `doc-code-copy` — which is what a # site's stylesheet restyles it by. The hook on this block's root (`copy_hook/0`) answers the # button: it copies the window's code, marks the button `data-copied` for a moment, and puts # `copied_text` in `doc-code-status` for a screen reader. # # A BLOCK OF MORE LINES THAN `code_lines` IS CUT AT THAT MANY: the window carries # `data-collapsible` and `data-collapse-lines`, its `
` the id `id`, and a foot under it holds
# the `doc-code-expand` button that shows all of it, saying `expand_text` with its number of lines
# and, once shown, `collapse_text`. The hook answers that button too; the cut is the stylesheet's.
language = escaped(code_language(block))
lines = code_lines(block)
collapsible = labels.lines > 0 and lines > labels.lines

IO.iodata_to_binary([
  ~s(
),
  ~s(
),
  ~s(),
  language,
  "",
  ~s(",
  ~s(),
  "
",
  (collapsible && String.replace_prefix(block, "),
       ~s(",
       "
"
     ]) || [],
  ""
])

helpers.name: code_lines
helpers.code:
# HOW MANY LINES A CODE BLOCK HOLDS, read off its text; a line break that ends it starts none.
block
|> String.replace(~r/<[^>]*>/, "")
|> String.trim()
|> String.split("\n")
|> length()

helpers.name: collapse_lines
helpers.code:
# THE LINES A LONG CODE BLOCK IS CUT AT: one of those the kit's stylesheet draws a cut for, else
# 16; 0 cuts none.
case assigns[:code_lines] do
  lines when lines in [0, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32] -> lines
  _other -> 16
end

helpers.name: code_language
helpers.code:
# THE LANGUAGE A CODE BLOCK IS WRITTEN IN, off the `language-` class its `<code>` — or its `<pre>` —
# carries: "heex" for `<pre class="highlight"><code class="language-heex">`. A block that names
# none has none.
opening =
  case Regex.run(~r/\A<pre(?:\s[^>]*)?>\s*(?:<code(?:\s[^>]*)?>)?/s, block) do
    [found] -> found
    nil -> ""
  end

named = ~r/\sclass="(?:[^"]*\s)?language-([A-Za-z0-9_+#.-]+)/

case Regex.run(named, opening, capture: :all_but_first) do
  [language] -> String.downcase(language)
  nil -> ""
end

helpers.name: escaped
helpers.code:
value
|> to_string()
|> Phoenix.HTML.html_escape()
|> Phoenix.HTML.safe_to_string()

helpers.name: copy_hook
helpers.code:
# THE NAME THE BROWSER KNOWS THIS KIT'S `doc-code-copy` HOOK BY, the hook that answers the button on
# every code window this block draws (`code_window/2`). It is installed with these components, so it
# is this site's hook when they are — `MishkaDocCodeCopy` on a site named mishka — and
# `GlobalDocCodeCopy` when they were installed for every site. The name comes from the rule the
# site's JavaScript is built with, so the two cannot disagree.
MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.Compilers.JavaScriptCompiler.browser_name(
  %{name: "doc-code-copy", is_global: is_nil(site_id())},
  site_name()
)

helpers.name: tabs_hook
helpers.code:
# THE NAME THE BROWSER KNOWS THIS KIT'S `doc-tabs` HOOK BY, the hook that keeps the address bar in
# step with the tab pressed. It is installed with these components, so it is this site's hook when
# they are — `MishkaDocTabs` on a site named mishka — and `GlobalDocTabs` when they were installed
# for every site. The name comes from the rule the site's JavaScript is built with, so the two
# cannot disagree.
MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.Compilers.JavaScriptCompiler.browser_name(
  %{name: "doc-tabs", is_global: is_nil(site_id())},
  site_name()
)

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
# A TAB IS NOT ANOTHER PAGE. Pressing one asks this block for nothing but the tab shown
# (`handle_event/3`), and the page is not read for it. `url_tab` is the tab the URL asked for the last
# time this block was drawn, so a URL that asks for another tab moves the tab shown to it; anything
# else — another page, another version, another key — reads the page again, and the page drawn again
# by its parent with the URL it had keeps the tab the reader pressed.
tab = asked_tab(socket.assigns)
asked = asked_page(socket.assigns)

case {socket.assigns[:loaded_with], socket.assigns[:url_tab]} do
  {^asked, url} when url != tab ->
    Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, shown_tab: tab, url_tab: tab)

  {^asked, ^tab} ->
    socket
    |> read_page()
    |> wait_for_extras()

  _read_again ->
    socket
    |> read_page()
    |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loaded_with: asked, shown_tab: tab, url_tab: tab)
    |> wait_for_extras()
end

helpers.name: read_page
helpers.code:
assigns = socket.assigns
language = asked_language(assigns)
slug = asked_workspace(assigns)
path = asked_path(assigns)
workspace = workspace_row(slug, path, language, trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) != "")
# THE URL NAMED A DOCUMENT AND NOTHING ANSWERS IS A MISSING PAGE, not a page with a notice on it —
# the same answer `MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError` gives everywhere else in this CMS,
# which LiveView converts exactly as a controller does.
#
# ONLY WHEN THE URL NAMED IT: a block PINNED to a document by its author — see `asked_workspace/1` —
# is their content to fix, and taking the page down for it would be the worse answer.
if workspace == nil and page_subject?(assigns) do
  missing!(socket)
end

versions = versions_of(workspace)
version = pick_version(versions, from_url(assigns, :version_param))
latest = latest_of(versions)
sections = sections_of(version, assigns[:current_user])
wanted = from_url(assigns, :section_param)
# NOTHING ASKED IS THE DOCUMENT'S OWN ADDRESS, which draws the version's front page when it has one
# and the landing when it has not.
found = section_at_path(sections, wanted)
section = (found && section_body(found, assigns[:current_user])) || nil
# AND A SECTION IT NAMED, on the page the document itself is the subject of. An author who PINNED a
# document has put this block on a page of their own — a stray `?section=` in the URL is a bad link
# into their page, not a missing page, and taking the whole thing down for it would be the worse
# answer. The same line the blog draws between the URL's subject and an author's choice.
if section == nil and wanted != "" and page_subject?(assigns) do
  missing!(socket)
end

# EVERY NOTE IS READ, drawn or not: the page's headings are named clear of the notes' anchors,
# and `doc-toc` names them the same way whatever either block shows.
shown_notes? = assigns[:show_notes] not in [nil, false]
notes = (section && notes_of(section, assigns[:current_user], shown_notes?)) || []
anchors = note_anchors(notes)
{previous, next} = neighbours(reading_order(sections), section)
# WHAT THE BUTTON ON EACH CODE BLOCK SAYS, from this block's own attributes (`code_window/2`).
labels = %{
  copy: assigns[:copy_text],
  copied: assigns[:copied_text],
  label: assigns[:copy_label],
  lines: collapse_lines(assigns),
  expand: assigns[:expand_text],
  collapse: assigns[:collapse_text]
}

placement = placement(section, assigns)
# THE NUMBER EVERY `{{doc.version}}` OF THE TEXT AND OF ITS NOTES IS DRAWN AS (`with_version/2`).
number = version && version.version_number
# WHERE THE PAGE IS AND WHICH HOST THE SITE ANSWERS ON, which `clean/2` tells the pages of this site
# by when it makes the links to them live.
links = %{
  current:
    section &&
      own_href(
        assigns[:doc_base],
        workspace,
        sections,
        section,
        trimmed(assigns[:lang_param]),
        %{}
      ),
  host: site_host()
}

Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
  document: workspace,
  version: version,
  latest: latest,
  sections: sections,
  section: section,
  body:
    (section &&
       code_windows(
         placed_cards(
           with_heading_ids(
             with_version(
               example_sources(clean(section.rendered_content, links), "section/#{section.id}"),
               number
             ),
             Map.values(anchors)
           ),
           placement
         ),
         labels,
         "#{assigns[:id]}-body"
       )) || "",
  notes:
    (shown_notes? && note_blocks(notes, anchors, labels, assigns[:id], placement, number, links)) ||
      [],
  crumbs: (assigns[:show_breadcrumb] && crumbs_to(sections, section)) || [],
  previous: previous,
  next: next,
  updated_at: updated_at(workspace, section),
  language: (workspace && workspace.language) || language,
  asked_document: (path != "" && path) || slug,
  wanted_slug: wanted,
  extras: page_extras(assigns, workspace, version, latest, sections, section)
)

helpers.name: updated_at
helpers.code:
# WHEN WHAT THIS ADDRESS SHOWS LAST CHANGED, to the second, the date its head gives as its
# `dateModified`: a page's own — the newest of the page, its notes and the archiving of one — and
# the document's at the document's own address, where its version's front page is drawn. `nil` when
# neither is known.
at =
  case section do
    %{front_page: false, last_modified_at: changed} -> changed
    _front_page_or_none -> document && document.updated_at
  end

case at do
  %DateTime{} -> DateTime.truncate(at, :second)
  _unknown -> nil
end

helpers.name: asked_page
helpers.code:
# EVERYTHING A READ OF THE PAGE IS MADE FROM, the tab aside (`load/1`).
key = tab_key(assigns)

params =
  case assigns[:params] do
    map when is_map(map) -> Map.delete(map, key)
    other -> other
  end

assigns
|> Map.take([
  :workspace,
  :path,
  :workspace_param,
  :section_param,
  :version_param,
  :lang,
  :lang_param,
  :doc_base,
  :show_breadcrumb,
  :show_notes,
  :copy_text,
  :copied_text,
  :copy_label,
  :code_lines,
  :expand_text,
  :collapse_text,
  :current_user,
  :tab_param
])
|> Map.put(:params, params)

helpers.name: tab_key
helpers.code:
# THE URL KEY THE TAB TRAVELS UNDER; an empty one is `tab`, since a tab bar nothing can switch is
# no tab bar.
case trimmed(assigns[:tab_param]) do
  "" -> "tab"
  key -> key
end

helpers.name: asked_tab
helpers.code:
# THE TAB THE URL ASKS FOR, by its id. Nothing asked is the page's own text.
key = tab_key(assigns)

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^key => asked} when is_binary(asked) -> trimmed(asked)
  _nothing_asked -> ""
end

helpers.name: open_tab
helpers.code:
# THE TAB SHOWN: the one the URL asks for when a plugin added it, else "" — the page's own text.
Enum.find_value(extras.tabs, "", &(&1.id == shown && &1.id))

helpers.name: page_extras
helpers.args: assigns, document, version, latest, sections, section
helpers.code:
# WHAT PLUGINS ADD TO THE PAGE — facts under its title and tabs beside its text — asked on
# `document:page:extras` (the kit's own documentation names the shapes), with each tab's link.
# Nothing is asked without a document.
case document do
  nil ->
    %{header: [], tabs: [], pending: [], asked: nil, docs_href: nil}

  found ->
    asked = extras_asked(found, version, sections, section)

    asked
    |> ask_extras()
    |> Map.put(:asked, asked)
    |> extras_links(assigns, found, version, latest, sections, section)
end

helpers.name: ask_extras
helpers.code:
# THE PLUGINS' ANSWER, in the shapes the template draws, and the PubSub topics it names for what is
# still being fetched. An event that cannot run hands back the empty lists it was handed, and an
# answer of any other shape adds nothing.
answer = MishkaInstaller.Event.Hook.call("document:page:extras", asked)

case answer do
  %{header: header, tabs: tabs} when is_list(header) and is_list(tabs) ->
    shown = tabs |> Enum.flat_map(&tab_given(&1)) |> Enum.uniq_by(& &1.id)

    %{
      header: Enum.flat_map(header, &fact_given(&1)),
      tabs: shown,
      pending:
        Enum.uniq(topic_of(Map.get(answer, :pending)) ++ Enum.flat_map(shown, &List.wrap(&1.pending)))
    }

  _not_an_answer ->
    %{header: [], tabs: [], pending: []}
end

helpers.name: extras_links
helpers.args: extras, assigns, document, version, latest, sections, section
helpers.code:
# EACH TAB'S LINK: the page with the tab's id under the tab key, and the page's other URL keys.
query =
  assigns
  |> kept_query()
  |> Map.merge(version_query(version, latest, assigns[:version_param]))

href = fn extra ->
  own_href(assigns[:doc_base], document, sections, section, assigns[:lang_param], extra)
end

extras
|> Map.put(:tabs, Enum.map(extras.tabs, &Map.put(&1, :href, href.(Map.put(query, tab_key(assigns), &1.id)))))
|> Map.put(:docs_href, href.(query))

helpers.name: topic_of
helpers.code:
# THE PUBSUB TOPIC A PLUGIN NAMES FOR WHAT IT IS STILL FETCHING, on `MishkaCmsCore.PubSub`.
case pending do
  %{topic: topic} when is_binary(topic) and topic != "" -> [topic]
  _no_topic -> []
end

helpers.name: pending_wait
helpers.code:
case assigns[:pending_wait] do
  wait when is_integer(wait) and wait > 0 -> wait
  _unset -> 120_000
end

helpers.name: wait_for_extras
helpers.code:
# WHAT A PLUGIN IS STILL FETCHING IS DRAWN WHEN IT ARRIVES. One task subscribes to the topics the
# answer named, asks once more — the fetch may have ended before it subscribed — and otherwise
# waits for the next word on them, up to `pending_wait`, then asks again. Nothing polls: whoever
# fetches announces it once, and every page waiting hears it.
extras = socket.assigns.extras

case extras.pending != [] and Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  false ->
    socket

  true ->
    asked = extras.asked
    topics = extras.pending
    wait = pending_wait(socket.assigns)

    MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(socket, :extras, fn ->
      Enum.each(topics, &Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(MishkaCmsCore.PubSub, &1))

      case ask_extras(asked) do
        %{pending: []} = answered ->
          {:answered, asked, answered}

        _still_fetching ->
          receive do
            _announced -> {:answered, asked, ask_extras(asked)}
          after
            wait -> {:timed_out, asked}
          end
      end
    end)
end

helpers.name: handle_async
helpers.code:
# AN ANSWER FOR THE PAGE STILL BEING READ is drawn, and waited on again while something in it is
# still being fetched; one for a page read before is dropped.
assigns = socket.assigns

case assigns.extras.asked == asked do
  false ->
    {:noreply, socket}

  true ->
    extras =
      answered
      |> Map.put(:asked, asked)
      |> extras_links(
        assigns,
        assigns.document,
        assigns.version,
        assigns.latest,
        assigns.sections,
        assigns.section
      )

    {:noreply, socket |> Phoenix.Component.assign(:extras, extras) |> wait_for_extras()}
end

helpers.name: handle_async
handle_async
helpers.code: {:noreply, Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :extras, unfetched(socket.assigns.extras))}

helpers.name: unfetched
extras_asked
helpers.code:
# WHAT A PLUGIN IS TOLD OF THE PAGE: its site, its document, the version shown, and the page read —
# with its address under the document and the pages and groups above it, nearest last; `nil` on the
# document's landing — beside the two lists it adds to.
paths = section_paths(sections)

page =
  case section do
    nil ->
      nil

    %{id: id} = read ->
      %{
        slug: read.slug,
        title: read.title,
        path: Enum.join(Map.get(paths, id, [read.slug]), "/"),
        parents:
          Enum.map(
            crumbs_to(sections, read),
            &%{slug: &1.slug, title: &1.title, group: &1.group_heading == true}
          )
      }
  end

%{
  site_id: site_id(),
  document: %{slug: document.slug, path: document.path, language: document.language},
  version: version && version.version_number,
  page: page,
  header: [],
  tabs: []
}

helpers.name: own_href
helpers.args: base, document, sections, section, lang_param, extra
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF THE PAGE BEING READ — the landing's when it reads none — with `extra` as its query:
# where each tab leads. A page with no address in this site's languages keeps the one it is read
# at, and only its query changes.
segments =
  case section do
    nil -> []
    %{id: id, slug: slug} -> Map.get(section_paths(sections), id, [slug])
  end

case document_href(base, document, segments, lang_param, extra) do
  nil -> "?" <> URI.encode_query(extra)
  path -> path
end

helpers.name: kept_query
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE'S OTHER URL KEYS, which a tab keeps: every key the page handed over but the ones this
# block writes itself — the document, the page, the version, the language and the tab — and the
# language a base carries as a segment.
own =
  [:workspace_param, :section_param, :version_param, :lang_param]
  |> Enum.map(&trimmed(assigns[&1]))
  |> Kernel.++([tab_key(assigns)])
  |> Kernel.++((":lang" in String.split(to_string(assigns[:doc_base]), "/") && ["lang"]) || [])

case assigns[:params] do
  params when is_map(params) ->
    for {key, value} <- params,
        is_binary(key) and is_binary(value),
        key not in own,
        into: %{},
        do: {key, value}

  _no_params ->
    %{}
end

helpers.name: plain
helpers.code:
# A WORD A PLUGIN HANDS OVER, AS TEXT: a string, a number or an atom. Anything else, and an empty
# string, is no word. The template escapes it.
case value do
  nil -> nil
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> (String.trim(binary) != "" && binary) || nil
  number when is_number(number) -> to_string(number)
  atom when is_atom(atom) -> Atom.to_string(atom)
  _not_a_word -> nil
end

helpers.name: tone_of
helpers.code:
# A TONE IS A WORD A STYLESHEET KEYS ON, as `data-tone`: lower-case letters, digits and `-`. Any
# other is `neutral`.
word = plain(tone) || "neutral"

case Regex.match?(~r/\A[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}\z/, word) do
  true -> word
  false -> "neutral"
end

helpers.name: safe_href
helpers.code:
# AN ADDRESS A PLUGIN'S LINK MAY LEAD TO: http or https with a host, or a path on this site. Any
# other — javascript:, data:, //elsewhere — draws no link.
case plain(href) do
  nil ->
    nil

  address ->
    case URI.parse(address) do
      %URI{scheme: scheme, host: host} when scheme in ["http", "https"] and is_binary(host) and host != "" ->
        address

      %URI{scheme: nil, host: nil, path: "/" <> _rest} ->
        address

      _elsewhere ->
        nil
    end
end

helpers.name: link_rel
helpers.code:
# THE `rel` OF A LINK FACT: the link types its plugin gives (`nofollow`, `sponsored`, `noopener`),
# each lower-case letters and `-`, once, joined by a space, and in place of the default. With none
# given, an address off the site is `noopener noreferrer` and a path on it has no `rel`.
kinds =
  (plain(given) || "")
  |> String.downcase()
  |> String.split()
  |> Enum.filter(&Regex.match?(~r/\A[a-z][a-z-]{0,31}\z/, &1))
  |> Enum.uniq()

case {kinds, external} do
  {[], true} -> "noopener noreferrer"
  {[], false} -> nil
  {named, _either} -> Enum.join(named, " ")
end

helpers.name: badge_given
helpers.code:
case given do
  %{text: text} ->
    case plain(text) do
      nil -> []
      word -> [%{text: word, tone: tone_of(Map.get(given, :tone))}]
    end

  _not_a_badge ->
    []
end

helpers.name: fact_given
helpers.code:
# ONE FACT A PLUGIN PUTS UNDER THE TITLE, or in a tab's list, in the shape the template draws; a
# kind it does not draw, or one missing what it shows, is left out. `:pending` stands for the facts
# still being fetched.
case given do
  %{kind: :pending} ->
    [%{kind: :pending, label: nil, text: plain(Map.get(given, :text))}]

  %{kind: :badges, items: items} when is_list(items) ->
    case Enum.flat_map(items, &badge_given(&1)) do
      [] -> []
      badges -> [%{kind: :badges, label: plain(Map.get(given, :label)), items: badges}]
    end

  %{kind: kind, value: value} when kind in [:command, :text] ->
    case plain(value) do
      nil -> []
      word -> [%{kind: kind, label: plain(Map.get(given, :label)), value: word}]
    end

  %{kind: :link, href: href} ->
    case {safe_href(href), plain(Map.get(given, :text))} do
      {nil, _no_address} ->
        []

      {_address, nil} ->
        []

      {address, text} ->
        external = URI.parse(address).scheme != nil

        [
          %{
            kind: :link,
            label: plain(Map.get(given, :label)),
            href: address,
            text: text,
            external: external,
            rel: link_rel(Map.get(given, :rel), external)
          }
        ]
    end

  _not_a_fact ->
    []
end

helpers.name: tab_given
helpers.code:
# ONE TAB A PLUGIN ADDS BESIDE THE PAGE'S TEXT, or none. Its id is the word the URL carries —
# lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_` — and never `documentation`, the text's own.
with %{id: id, label: label} <- given,
     word when is_binary(word) <- plain(id),
     true <- Regex.match?(~r/\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\z/, word) and word != "documentation",
     name when is_binary(name) <- plain(label) do
  [tab_shape(word, name, given)]
else
  _not_a_tab -> []
end

helpers.name: tab_shape
helpers.code:
# A TAB WHOSE DATA IS STILL BEING FETCHED SAYS SO — and names the topic its fetch is announced on,
# `pending` — and one whose fetch failed says that; any other holds its blocks: `blocks`, or the
# one block it is itself.
shape = %{id: id, label: label, text: nil, failed_text: nil, pending: nil, blocks: []}

case given do
  %{state: :not_ready} ->
    %{
      shape
      | text: plain(Map.get(given, :text)),
        failed_text: plain(Map.get(given, :failed_text)),

#
# AND IT READS NOTHING. The filter narrows the tree this block already holds, so a keystroke is a
# render and not a query — which it was, once per letter, when the whole load ran again to notice.

helpers.name: trimmed
helpers.code:
case value do
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  nil -> ""
  other -> to_string(other)
