helpers.name: from_url
helpers.code:
# A CAPTURED SEGMENT AND A QUERY KEY ARRIVE THE SAME WAY. The runtime merges a page's captures into
# the same map as its query string, so /docs/:workspace and /docs?workspace= are read by one line —
# and `:lang` may sit in ANY segment of the path, because nothing here looks at position.
name = trimmed(assigns[key])

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^name => found} when name != "" and is_binary(found) -> trimmed(found)
  _no_params_or_key -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_workspace
helpers.code:
# THE AUTHOR'S CHOICE WINS OVER THE URL'S. A block pinned to one document is pinned: it sits on a
# page about that document, and a reader appending ?workspace= must not turn it into another.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> from_url(assigns, :workspace_param)
  pinned -> pinned
end

helpers.name: asked_path
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS THIS PAGE SERVES A DOCUMENT AT, when it is that document's own — /product/docs. A
# block pinned to a document by its slug is the author's choice for a page of their own, and keeps
# it.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:path])
  _pinned -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_language
helpers.code:
# HERE THE URL WINS, which is the opposite of every other key and is the point of a language: a page
# offered in four of them is one page, and the reader says which. `lang_param` is the one key the
# language travels under — read here, written onto every link below — so emptying it stops both, and
# that is how an author pins a page to one language, and how a page whose language is a path segment
# keeps the language out of its query strings.
case from_url(assigns, :lang_param) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:lang])
  asked -> asked
end

helpers.name: doc_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF AN EDITION, built by `site_path/2` for the site the page renders for — in the
# template and in the task a block reads in alike, because `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4`
# hands the task the page's site. Each segment is appended to the base, and a `:lang` in the base —
# in any position, /:lang/docs or /docs/:lang — is filled with the language of the edition being
# linked to, not the one the page is read in, which is the only way a link to an edition in ANOTHER
# language can be built. The address is the one the site's URL mode gives that language:
# /docs/<document> in a first language the site leaves unprefixed, /fa/docs/<document> in Persian. A
# base without the segment carries the language as a query key instead, so nothing appends it twice.
# An edition whose language this site does not publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than
# a link to a 404.
numbered = Enum.with_index(segments)
pattern = Enum.reduce(numbered, to_string(base), fn {_segment, at}, acc -> acc <> "/:segment#{at}" end)

captures =
  numbered
  |> Map.new(fn {segment, at} -> {"segment#{at}", to_string(segment)} end)
  |> Map.put("lang", trimmed(language))

case site_path(pattern, captures) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    in_path? = ":lang" in String.split(to_string(base), "/")

    query =
      case {in_path?, trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
        {false, key, code} when key != "" and code != "" -> Map.put(extra, key, code)
        _carried_by_the_path_or_not_asked_for -> extra
      end

    case URI.encode_query(query) do
      "" -> path
      encoded -> path <> "?" <> encoded
    end
end

helpers.name: document_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A DOCUMENT, OR OF ONE OF ITS PAGES. A document with an Address of its own is read
# there and its pages under it — /product/docs/headless/switch — and that address is one edition's,
# so no `?lang=` is written onto it; any other is read under the base, by its slug.
case document do
  %{path: own} when is_binary(own) and own != "" ->
    doc_href(own, segments, document.language, "", extra)

  _read_by_its_slug ->
    doc_href(base, [document.slug | segments], document.language, lang_param, extra)
end

helpers.name: item_links
helpers.args: items, sections, base, document, lang_param, extra
helpers.code:
# EACH ITEM WITH THE ADDRESS OF ITS PAGE, or `nil` where it has none — a document in a language
# this site does not publish (`doc_href/5`), or a group with no page of its own — so the template
# draws that item as a word rather than as a link to nothing. A page's address holds the pages it is
# filed under (`section_paths/1`).
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.map(items, fn item ->
  href =
    case {document, item.group? and item.section.group_page != true} do
      {nil, _no_document} ->
        nil

      {_document, true} ->
        nil

      {found, false} ->
        document_href(
          base,
          found,
          Map.get(paths, item.section.id, [item.section.slug]),
          lang_param,
          extra
        )
    end

  {item, href}
end)

helpers.name: only_language
helpers.code:
# A PAGE WRITTEN IN ONE LANGUAGE SERVES THAT LANGUAGE'S EDITION AND NO OTHER. A slug names one
# document per site whatever language it is written in, so without this /fa/docs/<english-slug>
# answers the English document inside a Persian, right-to-left page, with nothing saying the URL was
# wrong. Left empty the block sits on a page that does not address languages at all, and the slug
# decides on its own.
require Ash.Query

case wanted do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)

helpers.name: workspace_row
helpers.code:
# A DOCUMENT IS FOUND BY THE ADDRESS ITS OWN PAGES SERVE IT AT — `path` — and by its slug
# everywhere else. A slug the URL names finds only a document with no address of its own: one that
# has an address is read there and nowhere else, so /docs/<its slug> is a missing page. A slug the
# author PINNED — see `asked_workspace/1` — finds the document wherever it is read.
require Ash.Query

wanted =
  case {trimmed(path), trimmed(slug)} do
    {"", ""} -> nil
    {"", by_slug} when pinned -> {:pinned, by_slug}
    {"", by_slug} -> {:slug, by_slug}
    {address, _slug} -> {:path, address}
  end

case wanted do
  nil ->
    {:ok, nil}

  {by, value} ->
    # AS THE SYSTEM, since a page whose own lock opens is drawn inside a document that does not.
    query =
      MishkaDocument.Workspace
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
      |> only_language(language)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :slug, :path, :language])

    case by do
      :pinned -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value)
      :slug -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value and is_nil(path))
      :path -> Ash.Query.filter(query, path == ^value)
    end
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
    |> first_row()
end

helpers.name: versions_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY VERSION A READER MAY BE SENT TO, resolved through the public read rather than by id. That is
# what keeps a draft version out: `?v=` names a NUMBER, and a number that is not in this list is not
# a version this document publishes, whoever typed it.
# AS THE SYSTEM, as `workspace_row/2` reads the document.
require Ash.Query

case workspace do
  nil ->
    {:ok, []}

  %{id: id} ->
    with {:ok, found} <-
           MishkaDocument.WorkspaceVersion
           |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
           |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_id == ^id)
           |> Ash.Query.select([
             :id,
             :version_number,
             :is_latest_for_version,
             :published_at,
             :inserted_at
           ])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      {:ok, Enum.sort_by(found, &{moment(&1.published_at), moment(&1.inserted_at), &1.id}, :desc)}
    end
end

helpers.code:

# editor marked latest — falling back to the most recently published when nobody has.
Enum.find(versions, & &1.is_latest_for_version) || List.first(versions)

helpers.name: sections_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY APPROVED PAGE OF THE VERSION, unpaged: this list IS the document's contents, and one that
# stopped at the twentieth would silently hide the rest of a thirty-page manual.
require Ash.Query

case version do
  nil ->
    {:ok, []}

  %{id: id} ->
    with {:ok, found} <-
           MishkaDocument.Section
           |> Ash.Query.for_read(
             :public_list_at_workspace_version,
             %{workspace_version_id: id},
             read_as(visitor)
           )
           |> Ash.Query.select([
             :id,
             :title,
             :slug,
             :order_position,
             :parent_section_id,
             :front_page,
             :group_heading,
             :group_page
           ])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      {:ok, Enum.sort_by(found, &{&1.order_position || 0, &1.title, &1.id})}
    end
end

helpers.name: rooted?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER WALKING UP FROM A PAGE EVER REACHES THE TOP. A pair of pages filed under each other is
# reachable from neither end, and a tree built without asking would either drop both of them out of
# the contents or walk between them for ever. Twenty steps is deeper than any manual and cheap.
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _gone} ->
    true

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    false

  {%{parent_section_id: nil}, _at_the_top} ->
    true

  {%{parent_section_id: parent}, _keep_going} ->
    case Map.get(by_id, parent) do
      nil -> true
      found -> rooted?(by_id, found, depth + 1)
    end
end

helpers.name: effective_parent
helpers.code:
# THE PARENT A PAGE IS DRAWN UNDER, which is not always the parent it names. A parent still waiting
# on a review is not published, and hanging its children off it would drop them out of the contents
# altogether — so they surface at the top instead, and so does anything in a loop.
parent = section.parent_section_id

cond do
  is_nil(parent) -> nil
  not Map.has_key?(by_id, parent) -> nil
  not rooted?(by_id, section, 0) -> nil
  true -> parent
end

helpers.name: section_paths
helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE'S OWN PART OF ITS ADDRESS — the slugs of the pages it is drawn under, then its own:
# headless/switch. The parents are the ones `effective_parent/2` draws it under, so a page's address
# is where the reader finds it in the contents. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent,
# so the same one under two parents is two addresses. The front page's is empty (`path_up/4`).
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})
Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, path_up(by_id, &1, [], 0)})

helpers.name: path_up
helpers.code:
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _at_the_top} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    gathered

  # A FRONT PAGE'S SLUG IS NO PART OF ANY ADDRESS. It is drawn at the document's own address, and the
  # pages filed under it sit directly under that.
  {%{front_page: true} = front, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, front)), gathered, depth + 1)

  # A GROUP WITH A PAGE OF ITS OWN IS READ AT ITS SLUG: the first step is the page being addressed,
  # and the group's own page is addressed by its slug.
  {%{group_heading: true, group_page: true} = group, 0} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), [group.slug | gathered], 1)

  # NOR A GROUP'S, above the page addressed: it is a heading, and the pages under it are addressed as
  # if it were not there.
  {%{group_heading: true} = group, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), gathered, depth + 1)

  {page, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, page)), [page.slug | gathered], depth + 1)
end

helpers.name: section_at_path
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE AN ADDRESS NAMES: the one whose own part of the address is exactly the one asked —
# headless/switch. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent, not in the document, so
# `switch` alone may be two pages. Nothing asked is the document's own address, which is the
# version's front page when it has one: the one page whose own part of the address is empty. A group
# is the page at an address only when it has a page of its own (`group_page`).
asked = String.split(trimmed(wanted), "/", trim: true)
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.find(
  sections,
  &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and Map.get(paths, &1.id) == asked)
)

helpers.name: ancestors
helpers.code:
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _gone} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    gathered

  {_node, _keep_going} ->
    case Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, section)) do
      nil -> gathered
      found -> ancestors(by_id, found, [found.id | gathered], depth + 1)
    end
end

helpers.name: open_ids
helpers.code:
case expand_all == true do
  true ->
    MapSet.new(sections, & &1.id)

  false ->
    case Map.get(by_id, active) do
      nil -> MapSet.new()
      found -> MapSet.new([found.id | ancestors(by_id, found, [], 0)])
    end
end

helpers.name: branch
helpers.code:
# A GROUP IS A HEADING OVER ITS PAGES, so it is always open: it has no page to open it on.
by_parent
|> Map.get(parent_id, [])
|> Enum.flat_map(fn section ->
  children = Map.get(by_parent, section.id, [])
  group? = section.group_heading == true
  opened = group? or MapSet.member?(open, section.id)

  item = %{
    section: section,
    depth: depth,
    active: section.id == active,
    parent?: children != [],
    open: opened,
    group?: group?
  }

  case opened and children != [] and depth < 20 do
    true -> [item | branch(by_parent, section.id, depth + 1, open, active)]
    false -> [item]
  end
end)

helpers.name: group_of
helpers.code:
# THE GROUP A PAGE IS LISTED UNDER: the nearest group above it, or `nil` for a page under none.
case {Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, section)), depth} do
  {nil, _at_the_top} -> nil
  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 -> nil
  {%{group_heading: true} = group, _found} -> group.id
  {parent, _keep_going} -> group_of(by_id, parent, depth + 1)
end

helpers.name: matching
helpers.code:
# A GROUP STAYS WHILE ONE OF ITS PAGES MATCHES, as the heading those pages are listed under, and
# goes when none does: its own title is no page to find — unless it has a page of its own.
needle = String.downcase(query)
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})

found =
  Enum.filter(
    sections,
    &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and
        String.contains?(String.downcase(&1.title), needle))
  )

under = Enum.group_by(found, &group_of(by_id, &1, 0))

item = fn section, depth ->
  %{
    section: section,
    depth: depth,
    active: section.id == active,
    parent?: false,
    open: false,
    group?: section.group_heading == true
  }
end

Enum.flat_map(sections, fn section ->
  cond do
    Map.has_key?(under, section.id) ->
      [item.(section, 0) | Enum.map(Map.fetch!(under, section.id), &item.(&1, 1))]

    section in Map.get(under, nil, []) ->
      [item.(section, 0)]

    true ->
      []
  end
end)

helpers.name: items_of
helpers.code:
# A FILTERED LIST IS A LIST AND NOT A TREE. A reader typing three letters is looking for one page,
# not for where it sits, and keeping the branches would bury the two matches under the four parents
# that had to be drawn to reach them.
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})

case query do
  "" ->
    by_parent = Enum.group_by(sections, &effective_parent(by_id, &1))
    branch(by_parent, nil, 0, open_ids(by_id, sections, active, expand_all), active)

  asked ->
    matching(sections, asked, active)
end

helpers.code:

helpers.name: handle_async
helpers.code: {:noreply, arrived(socket, result)}

helpers.name: handle_async
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT DIED TAKES THE BLOCK'S OWN STATE WITH IT AND NOTHING ELSE. The task is unlinked
# before it re-raises — see `Phoenix.LiveView.Async.do_async/5` — so the page around this block is
# still standing, and this is what it draws instead of the list.
{:noreply, Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, loading: false, failed: true)}

helpers.name: site_name
helpers.code:
# THE SITE'S NAME, NOT ITS ID, because that is what a component is addressed by: the runtime hashes
# a module out of (component name, site name). Every `<.component …/>` below draws a sibling of this
# one, which lives on the same site as this one and nowhere else.
__MODULE__.__component_information__([:private, :site])

helpers.name: asked
helpers.code:
%{
  visitor: assigns[:current_user],
  workspace: asked_workspace(assigns),
  pinned: trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) != "",
  path: asked_path(assigns),
  language: asked_language(assigns),
  version: from_url(assigns, :version_param),
  section: from_url(assigns, :section_param),

helpers.name: fetch
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT FAILS ENDS HERE AS `{:error, _}`, which `arrived/2` draws as the block's error.
with {:ok, workspace} <- workspace_row(asked.workspace, asked.path, asked.language, asked.pinned),
     {:ok, versions} <- versions_of(workspace),
     version = pick_version(versions, asked.version),
     {:ok, sections} <- sections_of(version, asked.visitor) do
  {:ok,
   %{
     document: workspace,
     version: version,
     latest: latest_of(versions),
     sections: sections,
     active:
       case section_at_path(sections, asked.section) do
         nil -> nil
         found -> found.id
       end
   }}
end

helpers.name: arrived
helpers.code:
socket =
  Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
    loading: false,
    failed: false,
    document: data.document,
    version: data.version,
    latest: data.latest,
    sections: data.sections,
    active: data.active
  )

Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :items, narrowed(socket, socket.assigns[:query]))

helpers.name: arrived
helpers.code: Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, loading: false, failed: true, sections: [], active: nil, items: [])

helpers.name: narrowed
helpers.code:
# THE TREE THE READER SEES, WHICH IS NOT WHAT WAS READ. The filter narrows what this block
# already holds, so the entries are worked out here — by the load when it lands, and by the filter
# on every keystroke — rather than being read again to notice a letter.
items_of(
  socket.assigns[:sections],
  trimmed(query),
  socket.assigns[:active],
  socket.assigns[:expand_all]
)

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.
socket.private[:runtime_cold] == true

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        # IN THE PAGE'S SITE AND LOCALE: `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4` hands the task both, so
        # `site_path/2` and `t/1` answer in it what they answer in the template.
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:contents, fn -> fetch(asked) end)
    end
end

helpers.name: scroll_hook
helpers.code:
# THE NAME THE BROWSER KNOWS THIS KIT'S `doc-sidebar-scroll` HOOK BY, the hook that keeps these
# contents where the reader left them when a link leads to the next page. It is installed with
# these components, so it is this site's hook when they are — `MishkaDocSidebarScroll` on a site
# named mishka — and `GlobalDocSidebarScroll` when they were installed for every site. The name
# comes from the rule the site's JavaScript is built with, so the two cannot disagree.
MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.Compilers.JavaScriptCompiler.browser_name(
  %{name: "doc-sidebar-scroll", is_global: is_nil(site_id())},
  site_name()
)

components.name: doc-toc
components.description: What is on the page being read — its headings and its notes — read in the background, as anchors into it.
components.template:
<.component :if={@loading and trimmed(@heading) != ""} component_name="doc-notice" site={site_name()} tone="loading" role="doc-toc-loading" text={@loading_text} /> <.component :if={@failed} component_name="doc-notice" site={site_name()} tone="error" role="doc-toc-error" text={@error_text} retry_text={@retry_text} target={@myself} />

{@heading}

  • entry.anchor} data-role="doc-toc-link" class="block text-sm leading-snug text-[#6d6a63] hover:text-[#5b57d6] hover:underline" > {entry.title}

opts.doc: The words above the list. Left empty, no heading is drawn.
A document's slug, to pin this block to one document. Left empty it reads the slug out of the URL under workspace_param.

The address of the document this page serves — the Address set on the document, /product/docs say — so the page reads that document rather than one a slug in the URL names, and its pages under it. The pages a document is given at its own address are written with it. A pinned workspace wins over it; left empty, the URL's slug decides.
The URL key a document's slug arrives under — a captured segment of the page's path, or a query key.

The URL key a page's address under its document arrives under — headless/switch, which a *section capture holds. Nothing under it means the document's own address: the page marked as its version's front page, whose headings are listed, else the landing, which has no table of contents of its own.
The URL key a version number arrives under. Nothing under it, or a version this document does not publish, means the latest.

The language this page is written in. A slug names one edition per site whatever language it is in, so naming the language here is what stops an English page's contents appearing beside a Persian one. Left empty the slug decides on its own.

The query key the language travels under: a reader's ?lang= replaces the language above. Leave it empty on a site whose language is a path segment, and to pin the block to one language. Empty it too on a documentation path that names no language — /docs/<document>/<page> — because a reader's ?lang= narrows the lookup to that language's edition, and a slug names one document per site whatever language it is in: a shared link carrying a stray one then finds nothing.
The page's own URL keys — its query string and its captured segments — handed straight through.

Where documents with no address of their own live — /docs, say, under which a page is reached as /docs/<document>/<page>. Write the language into it as :lang — /:lang/docs — on a site whose language is a path segment, and every link is the address the site's URL mode gives the language it leads to. A document with an Address of its own is linked there instead, its pages under it.
List the headings inside the page's own text.
List the notes filed under the page. On most pages these are the body of it, so they are most of this list.
How many entries it takes before the list is worth drawing. Under this many, nothing is drawn — a column headed On this page with one link in it is noise.
What a screen reader is told while the read is running.

opts.default: This page's contents could not be listed.
opts.doc: What a reader is told when the read failed.
The way out of a failed read.
The signed-in reader, handed down by the page as current_user. A page locked to permissions it does not hold, by its own lock or its document's, draws no contents; without one, no locked page does.

helpers.code: __MODULE__.__component_information__([:private, :site_id])

helpers.name: read_as
helpers.code:
# THE VISITOR THE READ IS FOR, AS ITS ACTOR, so a page locked to permissions it does not hold, by
# its own lock or its document's, draws no contents, and a page with nobody signed in reads as a
# guest. The tenant goes with it, because a public action that checks its tenant does so as it is

[actor: visitor, tenant: site_id()]

helpers.name: trimmed
helpers.code:
case value do
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  nil -> ""
  other -> to_string(other)
end

helpers.name: positive
helpers.code:
cond do
  is_integer(value) and value > 0 ->
    value

  is_binary(value) ->
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {number, _rest} when number > 0 -> number
      _not_a_number -> fallback
    end

  true ->
    fallback
end

helpers.name: from_url
helpers.code:
# A CAPTURED SEGMENT AND A QUERY KEY ARRIVE THE SAME WAY. The runtime merges a page's captures into
# the same map as its query string, so /docs/:workspace and /docs?workspace= are read by one line —
# and `:lang` may sit in ANY segment of the path, because nothing here looks at position.
name = trimmed(assigns[key])

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^name => found} when name != "" and is_binary(found) -> trimmed(found)
  _no_params_or_key -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_workspace
helpers.code:
# THE AUTHOR'S CHOICE WINS OVER THE URL'S. A block pinned to one document is pinned: it sits on a
# page about that document, and a reader appending ?workspace= must not turn it into another.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> from_url(assigns, :workspace_param)
  pinned -> pinned
end

helpers.name: asked_path
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS THIS PAGE SERVES A DOCUMENT AT, when it is that document's own — /product/docs. A
# block pinned to a document by its slug is the author's choice for a page of their own, and keeps
# it.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:path])
  _pinned -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_language
helpers.code:
# HERE THE URL WINS, which is the opposite of every other key and is the point of a language: a page
# offered in four of them is one page, and the reader says which. Emptying `lang_param` is how an
# author pins a page to one language, and how a page whose language is a path segment keeps the
# language out of its query strings.
case from_url(assigns, :lang_param) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:lang])
  asked -> asked
end

helpers.name: text_direction
helpers.code:
case trimmed(language) do
  code when code in ~w(fa ar he ur ps ckb dv yi) -> "rtl"
  _left_to_right_or_unknown -> "auto"
end

helpers.name: enough?
helpers.code:
# ONE LINK UNDER A HEADING THAT SAYS "ON THIS PAGE" IS NOT A TABLE OF CONTENTS. It is a link to the
# top of what the reader is already looking at, in a column that costs the page a third of its width.
length(entries) >= positive(min_entries, 2)

helpers.name: first_row
rows
moment
helpers.code:
# A TIME AS A NUMBER, because these are sorted in memory and two `%DateTime{}` structs compare by
# Erlang term order rather than by when they happened. A version nobody published sorts oldest.
case value do
  %DateTime{} = at -> DateTime.to_unix(at, :microsecond)
  _never -> 0
end

helpers.name: only_language
helpers.code:
# A PAGE WRITTEN IN ONE LANGUAGE SERVES THAT LANGUAGE'S EDITION AND NO OTHER. A slug names one
# document per site whatever language it is written in, so without this /fa/docs/<english-slug>
# answers the English document inside a Persian page, with nothing saying the URL was wrong.
require Ash.Query

case wanted do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: workspace_row
helpers.code:
# A DOCUMENT IS FOUND BY THE ADDRESS ITS OWN PAGES SERVE IT AT — `path` — and by its slug
# everywhere else. A slug the URL names finds only a document with no address of its own: one that
# has an address is read there and nowhere else, so /docs/<its slug> is a missing page. A slug the
# author PINNED — see `asked_workspace/1` — finds the document wherever it is read.
require Ash.Query

wanted =
  case {trimmed(path), trimmed(slug)} do
    {"", ""} -> nil
    {"", by_slug} when pinned -> {:pinned, by_slug}
    {"", by_slug} -> {:slug, by_slug}
    {address, _slug} -> {:path, address}
  end

case wanted do
  nil ->
    {:ok, nil}

  {by, value} ->
    # AS THE SYSTEM, since a page whose own lock opens is drawn inside a document that does not.
    query =
      MishkaDocument.Workspace
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
      |> only_language(language)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :language])

    case by do
      :pinned -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value)
      :slug -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value and is_nil(path))
      :path -> Ash.Query.filter(query, path == ^value)
    end
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
    |> first_row()
end

helpers.name: versions_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY VERSION A READER MAY BE SENT TO, resolved through the public read rather than by id. That is
# what keeps a draft version out: `?v=` names a NUMBER, and a number that is not in this list is not
# a version this document publishes, whoever typed it.
# AS THE SYSTEM, as `workspace_row/2` reads the document.
require Ash.Query

case workspace do
  nil ->
    {:ok, []}

  %{id: id} ->
    with {:ok, found} <-
           MishkaDocument.WorkspaceVersion
           |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
           |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_id == ^id)
           |> Ash.Query.select([
             :id,
             :version_number,
             :is_latest_for_version,
             :published_at,
             :inserted_at
           ])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      {:ok, Enum.sort_by(found, &{moment(&1.published_at), moment(&1.inserted_at), &1.id}, :desc)}
    end
end

helpers.name: latest_of
helpers.code:
# VERSION NUMBERS ARE TEXT, so "0.0.10" sorts under "0.0.9" and the newest is whichever one an
# editor marked latest — falling back to the most recently published when nobody has.
Enum.find(versions, & &1.is_latest_for_version) || List.first(versions)

helpers.name: pick_version
helpers.code:
case Enum.find(versions, &(&1.version_number == asked)) do
  nil -> latest_of(versions)
  found -> found
end

helpers.name: section_at
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE IS FOUND THROUGH ITS VERSION AND NEVER BY SLUG ALONE, and by its whole address: the
# version's pages are read as a tree, the one whose own part of the address is the one asked is
# picked — headless/switch, a slug being unique only among the pages under one parent, and nothing
# asked the front page — and that one alone is read for its text. The text is read for the headings
# (`headings?`); a block that lists no headings has all it needs in the page the tree gave.
require Ash.Query

case {version, trimmed(wanted)} do
  {nil, _no_version} ->
    {:ok, nil}

  {%{id: id}, asked} ->
    pages =
      MishkaDocument.Section
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(
        :public_list_at_workspace_version,
        %{workspace_version_id: id},
        read_as(visitor)
      )

    with {:ok, tree} <-
           pages
           |> Ash.Query.select([
             :id,
             :slug,
             :parent_section_id,
             :front_page,
             :group_heading,
             :group_page
           ])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      case {section_at_path(tree, asked), headings?} do
        {nil, _headings} ->
          {:ok, nil}

        {found, false} ->
          {:ok, found}

        {%{id: found}, true} ->
          pages
          |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^found)
          |> Ash.Query.load([:rendered_content])
          |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
          |> first_row()
      end
    end
end

helpers.name: rooted?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER WALKING UP FROM A PAGE EVER REACHES THE TOP. A pair of pages filed under each other is
# reachable from neither end, so without this both of them would be missing from the document's
# front page with nothing saying why. Twenty steps is deeper than any manual and cheap.
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _gone} ->
    true

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    false

  {%{parent_section_id: nil}, _at_the_top} ->
    true

  {%{parent_section_id: parent}, _keep_going} ->
    case Map.get(by_id, parent) do
      nil -> true
      found -> rooted?(by_id, found, depth + 1)
    end
end

helpers.name: effective_parent
helpers.code:
# THE PARENT A PAGE IS DRAWN UNDER, which is not always the parent it names. A parent still waiting
# on a review is not published, and hanging its children off it would drop them out of the document
# altogether — so they surface at the top instead, and so does anything in a loop. `doc-sidebar`
# decides the same question the same way, so the front page, the pager and the contents agree.
parent = section.parent_section_id

cond do
  is_nil(parent) -> nil
  not Map.has_key?(by_id, parent) -> nil
  not rooted?(by_id, section, 0) -> nil
  true -> parent
end

helpers.name: section_paths
helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE'S OWN PART OF ITS ADDRESS — the slugs of the pages it is drawn under, then its own:
# headless/switch. The parents are the ones `effective_parent/2` draws it under, so a page's address
# is where the reader finds it in the contents. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent,
# so the same one under two parents is two addresses. The front page's is empty (`path_up/4`).
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})
Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, path_up(by_id, &1, [], 0)})

helpers.name: path_up
helpers.code:
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _at_the_top} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    gathered

  # A FRONT PAGE'S SLUG IS NO PART OF ANY ADDRESS. It is drawn at the document's own address, and the
  # pages filed under it sit directly under that.
  {%{front_page: true} = front, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, front)), gathered, depth + 1)

  # A GROUP WITH A PAGE OF ITS OWN IS READ AT ITS SLUG: the first step is the page being addressed,
  # and the group's own page is addressed by its slug.
  {%{group_heading: true, group_page: true} = group, 0} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), [group.slug | gathered], 1)

  # NOR A GROUP'S, above the page addressed: it is a heading, and the pages under it are addressed as
  # if it were not there.
  {%{group_heading: true} = group, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), gathered, depth + 1)

  {page, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, page)), [page.slug | gathered], depth + 1)
end

helpers.name: section_at_path
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE AN ADDRESS NAMES: the one whose own part of the address is exactly the one asked —
# headless/switch. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent, not in the document, so
# `switch` alone may be two pages. Nothing asked is the document's own address, which is the
# version's front page when it has one: the one page whose own part of the address is empty. A group
# is the page at an address only when it has a page of its own (`group_page`).
asked = String.split(trimmed(wanted), "/", trim: true)
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.find(
  sections,
  &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and Map.get(paths, &1.id) == asked)
)

helpers.name: notes_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY APPROVED NOTE, unpaged, and in the same order `doc-section` draws them: each entry here is
# an anchor into that markup, and a list that stopped short would leave the rest of the page with
# nothing pointing at it.
require Ash.Query

case section do
  nil ->
    {:ok, []}

  %{id: id} ->
    with {:ok, found} <-
           MishkaDocument.Note
           |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
           |> Ash.Query.filter(section_id == ^id)
           |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :title, :order_position])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      {:ok, Enum.sort_by(found, &{&1.order_position || 0, &1.id})}
    end
end

helpers.name: clean
helpers.code:
# THE SAME SCRUB `doc-section` APPLIES, and it has to be the same one: the ids below are computed
# from what that scrub leaves behind, so a different one here would compute anchors for headings the
# page never drew.
case is_binary(content) do
  true -> HtmlSanitizeEx.html5(content)
  false -> ""
end

helpers.name: with_version
helpers.code:
# EVERY `{{doc.version}}` OF A PAGE'S TEXT — `{{ doc.version }}` too — IS `number`, the version the
# reader is reading, HTML-escaped: in its code blocks and in a marker's attributes as well, so an
# install line or a link to a release follows the version picked. `\{{doc.version}}` is drawn as
# `{{doc.version}}`. With no number, the text is handed back as it is. `doc-section`, `doc-toc` and
# `doc-section-cards` carry this word for word, and
# `MishkaDocumentWeb.Live.ExamplePreview.with_version/2` is the same rule.
case is_binary(html) and is_binary(number) and String.contains?(html, "{{") do
  false ->
    html

  true ->
    filled = number |> Phoenix.HTML.html_escape() |> Phoenix.HTML.safe_to_string()

    Regex.replace(~r/(\\?)\{\{\s*doc\.version\s*\}\}/u, html, fn whole, escape ->
      case escape do
        "" -> filled
        _escaped -> String.slice(whole, 1..-1//1)
      end
    end)
end

helpers.name: strip_tags
helpers.code:
value
|> to_string()
|> String.replace(~r/<[^>]*>/, " ")
|> String.replace(" ", " ")
|> String.replace("<", "<")
|> String.replace(">", ">")
|> String.replace(""", "\"")
|> String.replace("'", "'")
|> String.replace("&", "&")
|> String.replace(~r/\s+/u, " ")
|> String.trim()

helpers.name: anchor_slug
helpers.code:
# A TITLE'S OWN WORDS, IN ANY ALPHABET: lower case, every run of what is not a letter or a digit
# one `-`, none at either end, and `""` when nothing is left. `[^a-z0-9]` would empty a Persian or
# Arabic title, so letters and digits are matched by their Unicode category. `doc-section` and
# `doc-toc` carry this, `anchors_of/3`, `free_anchor/3` and `note_anchors/1` word for word, so a
# heading and a note are named by one rule in both.
text
|> to_string()
|> String.downcase()
|> String.replace(~r/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u, "-")
|> String.trim("-")

helpers.name: anchors_of
helpers.code:
# ONE ANCHOR PER TITLE, IN THE ORDER GIVEN: its slug (`anchor_slug/1`), or `<fallback>-<place>`
# counted from 1 when it has none, and never one in `taken` or minted before it — the second of a
# slug is `-2`, the third `-3` (`free_anchor/3`).
texts
|> Enum.with_index(1)
|> Enum.map_reduce(MapSet.new(taken), fn {text, place}, used ->
  base =
    case anchor_slug(text) do
      "" -> fallback <> "-" <> Integer.to_string(place)
      slug -> slug
    end

  anchor = free_anchor(base, used, 1)
  {anchor, MapSet.put(used, anchor)}
end)
|> elem(0)

helpers.name: free_anchor
helpers.code:
# `base` when no anchor in `used` is, else the first of `base-2`, `base-3`, … that is free.
candidate =
  case tried do
    1 -> base
    _later -> base <> "-" <> Integer.to_string(tried)
  end

case MapSet.member?(used, candidate) do
  true -> free_anchor(base, used, tried + 1)
  false -> candidate
end

helpers.name: note_anchors
helpers.code:
# THE ANCHOR OF EACH NOTE OF THE PAGE, BY ITS ID: the slug of its title, `#color-palette`, or
# `note-<place>` for a title with no letter or digit. `notes` are in the order the page draws
# them, which is the order the second note of one title is told apart in.
notes
|> Enum.map(& &1.id)
|> Enum.zip(anchors_of(Enum.map(notes, & &1.title), "note", []))
|> Map.new()

helpers.name: heading_entries
helpers.code:
# THE HEADINGS OF A PAGE, AND THE ID EACH ONE ANSWERS TO, minted by `anchors_of/3` clear of `taken`,
# the anchors the page's notes answer to. `doc-section` runs exactly this over exactly the same
# scrubbed markup and the same notes before writing those ids onto it, so the two agree on every
# anchor.
entries =
  ~r/<(h[23])(?:\s[^>]*)?>(.*?)<\/\1>/su
  |> Regex.scan(html)
  |> Enum.map(fn [_whole, tag, inner] -> %{text: strip_tags(inner), level: tag} end)

entries
|> Enum.map(& &1.text)
|> anchors_of("heading", taken)
|> Enum.zip_with(entries, fn id, entry -> Map.put(entry, :id, id) end)

helpers.name: entries_of
helpers.code:
anchors = note_anchors(notes)

headings =
  case show_headings == true and section != nil do
    true ->
      section.rendered_content
      |> clean()
      |> with_version(number)
      |> heading_entries(Map.values(anchors))
      |> Enum.map(&%{anchor: &1.id, title: &1.text, kind: &1.level})

    false ->
      []
  end

listed =
  case show_notes == true do
    true -> Enum.map(notes, &%{anchor: Map.fetch!(anchors, &1.id), title: &1.title, kind: "note"})
    false -> []
  end

headings ++ listed

helpers.code:
{:noreply,
 socket

helpers.name: handle_async
helpers.code: {:noreply, arrived(socket, result)}

helpers.name: handle_async
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT DIED TAKES THE BLOCK'S OWN STATE WITH IT AND NOTHING ELSE. The task is unlinked
# before it re-raises — see `Phoenix.LiveView.Async.do_async/5` — so the page around this block is
# still standing, and this is what it draws instead of the list.
{:noreply, Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, loading: false, failed: true)}

helpers.name: site_name
helpers.code:
# THE SITE'S NAME, NOT ITS ID, because that is what a component is addressed by: the runtime hashes
# a module out of (component name, site name). Every `<.component …/>` below draws a sibling of this
# one, which lives on the same site as this one and nowhere else.
__MODULE__.__component_information__([:private, :site])

helpers.name: asked
helpers.code:
%{
  visitor: assigns[:current_user],
  workspace: asked_workspace(assigns),
  pinned: trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) != "",
  path: asked_path(assigns),
  language: asked_language(assigns),
  version: from_url(assigns, :version_param),
  section: from_url(assigns, :section_param),
  show_headings: assigns[:show_headings] == true,
  show_notes: assigns[:show_notes] == true
}

helpers.name: fetch
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT FAILS ENDS HERE AS `{:error, _}`, which `arrived/2` draws as the block's error.
with {:ok, workspace} <- workspace_row(asked.workspace, asked.path, asked.language, asked.pinned),
     {:ok, versions} <- versions_of(workspace),
     version = pick_version(versions, asked.version),
     # NOTHING IS READ FOR A BLOCK THAT LISTS NOTHING: with no headings and no notes asked for, the
     # page they would come from is not looked for.
     listed? = asked.show_notes or asked.show_headings,
     {:ok, section} <-
       (listed? && section_at(version, asked.section, asked.visitor, asked.show_headings)) ||
         {:ok, nil},
     # THE NOTES ARE READ FOR THE HEADINGS TOO: a heading is named clear of the notes' anchors,
     # as `doc-section` names it.
     {:ok, notes} <- (listed? && notes_of(section, asked.visitor)) || {:ok, []} do
  {:ok,
   %{
     entries:
       entries_of(
         section,
         notes,
         asked.show_headings,
         asked.show_notes,
         version && version.version_number
       ),
     language: (workspace && workspace.language) || asked.language
   }}
end

helpers.name: arrived
helpers.code: Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, loading: false, failed: false, entries: data.entries, language: data.language)

helpers.name: arrived
helpers.code: Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, loading: false, failed: true, entries: [])

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.
socket.private[:runtime_cold] == true

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        # IN THE PAGE'S SITE AND LOCALE: `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4` hands the task both, so
        # `site_path/2` and `t/1` answer in it what they answer in the template.
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:entries, fn -> fetch(asked) end)
    end
end

helpers.code:
{:ok,
 Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
   asked: nil,

   version: nil,
   latest: nil,
   version_links: [],

helpers.name: update
helpers.code: {:ok, load(socket)}

helpers.name: site_id
helpers.code: __MODULE__.__component_information__([:private, :site_id])

helpers.name: read_as
helpers.code:
# THE VISITOR THE READ IS FOR, AS ITS ACTOR, so a document or a page of one locked to permissions
# it does not hold is left out of what is listed, and a page with nobody signed in reads as a guest.
# The tenant goes with it, because a public action that checks its tenant does so as it is prepared.
[actor: visitor, tenant: site_id()]

helpers.name: trimmed
helpers.code:
case value do
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  nil -> ""
  other -> to_string(other)
end

helpers.name: from_url
helpers.code:
# A CAPTURED SEGMENT AND A QUERY KEY ARRIVE THE SAME WAY. The runtime merges a page's captures into
# the same map as its query string, so /docs/:workspace and /docs?workspace= are read by one line —
# and `:lang` may sit in ANY segment of the path, because nothing here looks at position.
name = trimmed(assigns[key])

case assigns[:params] do
  %{^name => found} when name != "" and is_binary(found) -> trimmed(found)
  _no_params_or_key -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_workspace
helpers.code:
# THE AUTHOR'S CHOICE WINS OVER THE URL'S. A block pinned to one document is pinned: it sits on a
# page about that document, and a reader appending ?workspace= must not turn it into another.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> from_url(assigns, :workspace_param)
  pinned -> pinned
end

helpers.name: asked_path
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS THIS PAGE SERVES A DOCUMENT AT, when it is that document's own — /product/docs. A
# block pinned to a document by its slug is the author's choice for a page of their own, and keeps
# it.
case trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:path])
  _pinned -> ""
end

helpers.name: asked_language
helpers.code:
# HERE THE URL WINS, which is the opposite of every other key and is the point of a language: a page
# offered in four of them is one page, and the reader says which. Emptying `lang_param` is how an
# author pins a page to one language, and how a page whose language is a path segment keeps the
# language out of its query strings.
case from_url(assigns, :lang_param) do
  "" -> trimmed(assigns[:lang])
  asked -> asked
end

helpers.name: served?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER THIS SITE HAS A URL FOR AN EDITION — whether the address it is read under, its own or the
# base, makes one in its language (`site_path/2`, as `doc_href/5` builds one). A `:lang` capture
# answers `site.languages` alone, so a document translated into French on a site publishing English
# and Persian cannot be addressed here at all. An address with no `:lang` in it makes no language
# claim, so everything is addressable through it.
root =
  case edition do
    %{path: own} when is_binary(own) and own != "" -> own
    _read_by_its_slug -> base
  end

site_path(to_string(root), %{"lang" => trimmed(edition.language)}) != nil

helpers.name: doc_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF AN EDITION, built by `site_path/2` for the site the page renders for — in the
# template and in the task a block reads in alike, because `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4`
# hands the task the page's site. Each segment is appended to the base, and a `:lang` in the base —
# in any position, /:lang/docs or /docs/:lang — is filled with the language of the edition being
# linked to, not the one the page is read in, which is the only way a link to an edition in ANOTHER
# language can be built. The address is the one the site's URL mode gives that language:
# /docs/<document> in a first language the site leaves unprefixed, /fa/docs/<document> in Persian. A
# base without the segment carries the language as a query key instead, so nothing appends it twice.
# An edition whose language this site does not publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than
# a link to a 404.
numbered = Enum.with_index(segments)
pattern = Enum.reduce(numbered, to_string(base), fn {_segment, at}, acc -> acc <> "/:segment#{at}" end)

captures =
  numbered
  |> Map.new(fn {segment, at} -> {"segment#{at}", to_string(segment)} end)
  |> Map.put("lang", trimmed(language))

case site_path(pattern, captures) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    in_path? = ":lang" in String.split(to_string(base), "/")

    query =
      case {in_path?, trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
        {false, key, code} when key != "" and code != "" -> Map.put(extra, key, code)
        _carried_by_the_path_or_not_asked_for -> extra
      end

    case URI.encode_query(query) do
      "" -> path
      encoded -> path <> "?" <> encoded
    end
end

helpers.name: document_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A DOCUMENT, OR OF ONE OF ITS PAGES. A document with an Address of its own is read
# there and its pages under it — /product/docs/headless/switch — and that address is one edition's,
# so no `?lang=` is written onto it; any other is read under the base, by its slug.
case document do
  %{path: own} when is_binary(own) and own != "" ->
    doc_href(own, segments, document.language, "", extra)

  _read_by_its_slug ->
    doc_href(base, [document.slug | segments], document.language, lang_param, extra)
end

helpers.name: version_query
version_summary
helpers.code:
number = to_string((version && version.version_number) || "-")

case trimmed(version_text) do
  "" -> number
  _named -> "#{version_text}: #{number}"
end

helpers.name: text_direction
helpers.code:
case trimmed(language) do
  code when code in ~w(fa ar he ur ps ckb dv yi) -> "rtl"
  _left_to_right_or_unknown -> "auto"
end

helpers.name: first_row
rows
link_rows
helpers.code:
# A LINK THAT COULD NOT BE READ IS LEFT OUT, and the switch keeps the rest.
case rows(result) do
  {:ok, found} -> found
  {:error, _unreadable} -> []
end

helpers.name: moment
helpers.code:
# A TIME AS A NUMBER, because these are sorted in memory and two `%DateTime{}` structs compare by
# Erlang term order rather than by when they happened. A version nobody published sorts oldest.
case value do
  %DateTime{} = at -> DateTime.to_unix(at, :microsecond)
  _never -> 0
end

helpers.name: newest_first
helpers.code: Enum.sort_by(versions, &{moment(&1.published_at), moment(&1.inserted_at), &1.id}, :desc)

helpers.name: only_language
helpers.code:
# A PAGE WRITTEN IN ONE LANGUAGE SERVES THAT LANGUAGE'S EDITION AND NO OTHER. A slug names one
# document per site whatever language it is written in, so without this /fa/docs/<english-slug>
# answers the English document inside a Persian page, with nothing saying the URL was wrong.
require Ash.Query

case wanted do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: workspace_row
helpers.code:
# A DOCUMENT IS FOUND BY THE ADDRESS ITS OWN PAGES SERVE IT AT — `path` — and by its slug
# everywhere else. A slug the URL names finds only a document with no address of its own: one that
# has an address is read there and nowhere else, so /docs/<its slug> is a missing page. A slug the
# author PINNED — see `asked_workspace/1` — finds the document wherever it is read.
require Ash.Query

wanted =
  case {trimmed(path), trimmed(slug)} do
    {"", ""} -> nil
    {"", by_slug} when pinned -> {:pinned, by_slug}
    {"", by_slug} -> {:slug, by_slug}
    {address, _slug} -> {:path, address}
  end

case wanted do
  nil ->
    {:ok, nil}

  {by, value} ->
    # AS THE SYSTEM, since a page whose own lock opens is drawn inside a document that does not.
    query =
      MishkaDocument.Workspace
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
      |> only_language(language)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :slug, :path, :language, :language_group_id])

    case by do
      :pinned -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value)
      :slug -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug == ^value and is_nil(path))
      :path -> Ash.Query.filter(query, path == ^value)
    end
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
    |> first_row()
end

helpers.name: versions_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY VERSION A READER MAY BE SENT TO, resolved through the public read rather than by id. That is
# what keeps a draft or archived version out of this switch: it lists what this read answers with,
# so a number nobody published is a number nobody can be offered.
# AS THE SYSTEM, as `workspace_row/2` reads the document.
require Ash.Query

case workspace do
  nil ->
    {:ok, []}

  %{id: id} ->
    with {:ok, found} <-
           MishkaDocument.WorkspaceVersion
           |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, authorize?: false)
           |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_id == ^id)
           |> Ash.Query.select([
             :id,
             :version_number,
             :status,
             :is_latest_for_version,
             :published_at,
             :inserted_at
           ])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      {:ok, newest_first(found)}
    end
end

helpers.name: latest_of
helpers.code:
# VERSION NUMBERS ARE TEXT, so "0.0.10" sorts under "0.0.9" and the newest is whichever one an
# editor marked latest — falling back to the most recently published when nobody has.
Enum.find(versions, & &1.is_latest_for_version) || List.first(versions)

helpers.name: pick_version
helpers.code:
case Enum.find(versions, &(&1.version_number == asked)) do
  nil -> latest_of(versions)
  found -> found
end

helpers.name: page_at
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE IS FOUND THROUGH ITS VERSION AND NEVER BY SLUG ALONE, and by its whole address: the
# version's pages (`version_pages/2`) are read as a tree and the one whose own part of the address
# is the one asked is picked — headless/switch, a slug being unique only among the pages under one
# parent, and nothing asked the front page. It comes back with that address, which is what the entry
# for its own edition leads back to; `nil` where the version has no page at it.
case {version, trimmed(wanted)} do
  {nil, _no_version} ->
    nil

  {%{id: id}, asked} ->
    tree = Map.get(pages, id, [])

    case section_at_path(tree, asked) do
      nil -> nil
      found -> %{section: found, address: Map.get(section_paths(tree), found.id)}
    end
end

helpers.name: version_pages
helpers.code:
# THE PAGES OF EVERY VERSION ASKED FOR, IN ONE READ, by the id of the version: the page being read,
# its address in its own version and its address in every other are all found in these, so the
# switch reads the pages once rather than once for the version shown and again for all of them.
# Each version's pages come whole, because a page's address holds the pages it is filed under in
# that version.
require Ash.Query

case Enum.map(versions, & &1.id) do
  [] ->
    {:ok, %{}}

  wanted ->
    with {:ok, found} <-
           MishkaDocument.Section
           |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
           |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_version_id in ^wanted)
           |> Ash.Query.select([
             :id,
             :slug,
             :parent_section_id,
             :front_page,
             :group_heading,
             :group_page,
             :workspace_version_id,
             :section_lineage_id,
             :language_group_id
           ])
           |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
           |> rows() do
      {:ok, Enum.group_by(found, & &1.workspace_version_id)}
    end
end

helpers.name: rooted?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER WALKING UP FROM A PAGE EVER REACHES THE TOP. A pair of pages filed under each other is
# reachable from neither end, so without this both of them would be missing from the document's
# front page with nothing saying why. Twenty steps is deeper than any manual and cheap.
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _gone} ->
    true

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    false

  {%{parent_section_id: nil}, _at_the_top} ->
    true

  {%{parent_section_id: parent}, _keep_going} ->
    case Map.get(by_id, parent) do
      nil -> true
      found -> rooted?(by_id, found, depth + 1)
    end
end

helpers.name: effective_parent
helpers.code:
# THE PARENT A PAGE IS DRAWN UNDER, which is not always the parent it names. A parent still waiting
# on a review is not published, and hanging its children off it would drop them out of the document
# altogether — so they surface at the top instead, and so does anything in a loop. `doc-sidebar`
# decides the same question the same way, so the front page, the pager and the contents agree.
parent = section.parent_section_id

cond do
  is_nil(parent) -> nil
  not Map.has_key?(by_id, parent) -> nil
  not rooted?(by_id, section, 0) -> nil
  true -> parent
end

helpers.name: section_paths
helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE'S OWN PART OF ITS ADDRESS — the slugs of the pages it is drawn under, then its own:
# headless/switch. The parents are the ones `effective_parent/2` draws it under, so a page's address
# is where the reader finds it in the contents. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent,
# so the same one under two parents is two addresses. The front page's is empty (`path_up/4`).
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})
Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, path_up(by_id, &1, [], 0)})

helpers.name: path_up
helpers.code:
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _at_the_top} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    gathered

  # A FRONT PAGE'S SLUG IS NO PART OF ANY ADDRESS. It is drawn at the document's own address, and the
  # pages filed under it sit directly under that.
  {%{front_page: true} = front, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, front)), gathered, depth + 1)

  # A GROUP WITH A PAGE OF ITS OWN IS READ AT ITS SLUG: the first step is the page being addressed,
  # and the group's own page is addressed by its slug.
  {%{group_heading: true, group_page: true} = group, 0} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), [group.slug | gathered], 1)

  # NOR A GROUP'S, above the page addressed: it is a heading, and the pages under it are addressed as
  # if it were not there.
  {%{group_heading: true} = group, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), gathered, depth + 1)

  {page, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, page)), [page.slug | gathered], depth + 1)
end

helpers.name: section_at_path
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE AN ADDRESS NAMES: the one whose own part of the address is exactly the one asked —
# headless/switch. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent, not in the document, so
# `switch` alone may be two pages. Nothing asked is the document's own address, which is the
# version's front page when it has one: the one page whose own part of the address is empty. A group
# is the page at an address only when it has a page of its own (`group_page`).
asked = String.split(trimmed(wanted), "/", trim: true)
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.find(
  sections,
  &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and Map.get(paths, &1.id) == asked)
)

helpers.name: lineage_slugs
helpers.code:
# THE SAME PAGE IN EVERY VERSION, AT ITS ADDRESS THERE, out of the pages already read
# (`version_pages/2`). A page cloned forward keeps its `section_lineage_id`, so this is what "the
# same page" means across versions — and asking version by version would be a read per entry in the
# switch. Each version's pages come whole, because a page's address holds the pages it is filed
# under in that version.
case page do
  %{section: %{section_lineage_id: lineage}} when not is_nil(lineage) ->
    pages
    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {version_id, pages_of_version} ->
      case Enum.find(
             pages_of_version,
             &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and
                 &1.section_lineage_id == lineage)
           ) do
        nil -> []
        found -> [{version_id, Map.get(section_paths(pages_of_version), found.id)}]
      end
    end)
    |> Map.new()

  _no_page_or_no_lineage ->
    %{}
end

helpers.name: variants_of
helpers.code:
# EVERY EDITION OF THIS DOCUMENT, the one being read among them — and none at all where it is the
# only one. `SetLanguageGroupId` gives every document written here a group holding itself, so the
# nil clause below catches only a row an admin later emptied; without the last one, a document
# nobody has translated draws a switch offering the language it is already being read in, and pays
# the two reads under `language_links/5` to fill it.
require Ash.Query

case workspace do
  nil ->
    []

  %{language_group_id: nil} ->
    []

  %{language_group_id: group} ->
    MishkaDocument.Workspace
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(language_group_id == ^group)
    |> Ash.Query.sort(language: :asc)
    |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :slug, :path, :language])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> link_rows()
    |> case do
      [_the_only_edition] -> []
      editions -> editions
    end
end

helpers.name: latest_versions_of
helpers.code:
# THE VERSION EACH EDITION IS CURRENTLY ON. Editions number their versions on their own — Persian
# may be on 0.0.3 while English is on 0.0.6 — so a `?v=` never crosses a language switch, and each
# link lands on whatever that edition calls its latest.
require Ash.Query

case Enum.map(workspaces, & &1.id) do
  [] ->
    %{}

  wanted ->
    MishkaDocument.WorkspaceVersion
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_id in ^wanted)
    |> Ash.Query.select([
      :id,
      :workspace_id,
      :version_number,
      :is_latest_for_version,
      :published_at,
      :inserted_at
    ])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> link_rows()
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.workspace_id)
    |> Map.new(fn {workspace_id, found} -> {workspace_id, latest_of(newest_first(found))} end)
end

helpers.name: translated_slugs
helpers.code:
# THE SAME PAGE IN EVERY OTHER LANGUAGE, AT ITS ADDRESS THERE, IN ONE READ. Translations of one page
# share a `language_group_id`, and the slug is the fallback for an edition whose author never linked
# them — a Persian page called `installation` is still the Persian `installation`. Each version's
# pages come whole, because a page's address holds the pages it is filed under in that version.
require Ash.Query

case {version_ids, page} do
  {[], _no_versions} ->
    %{}

  {_ids, nil} ->
    %{}

  {wanted, %{section: %{slug: slug, language_group_id: group}}} ->
    MishkaDocument.Section
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.Query.filter(workspace_version_id in ^wanted)
    |> Ash.Query.select([
      :id,
      :slug,
      :parent_section_id,
      :front_page,
      :group_heading,
      :group_page,
      :workspace_version_id,
      :language_group_id
    ])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)
    |> link_rows()
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.workspace_version_id)
    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {version_id, pages} ->
      named = Enum.reject(pages, &(&1.group_heading == true and &1.group_page != true))
      linked = Enum.find(named, &(not is_nil(group) and &1.language_group_id == group))

      case linked || Enum.find(named, &(&1.slug == slug)) do
        nil -> []
        found -> [{version_id, Map.get(section_paths(pages), found.id)}]
      end
    end)
    |> Map.new()
end

helpers.name: landing_or_page
helpers.code:
# THE SAME PAGE WHERE THERE IS ONE, AND THE DOCUMENT'S FRONT PAGE WHERE THERE IS NOT. A page written
# after an older version was cut does not exist in it, and a link to an address that version never
# had would be a link to nothing.
document_href(base, workspace, address || [], lang_param, extra)

helpers.name: version_links
helpers.args: assigns, workspace, versions, addresses, current, latest
helpers.code:
# A VERSION OFFERED IS ONE IT CAN SWITCH TO — the rule `language_links/5` keeps: a version of a
# document in a language this site does not publish has no address (`doc_href/5`), and an entry
# leading nowhere in a menu whose whole purpose is to be clicked is dropped, the menu with it once
# none is left.
Enum.map(versions, fn version ->
  %{
    version: version,
    latest: latest != nil and version.id == latest.id,
    current: current != nil and version.id == current.id,
    href:
      landing_or_page(
        assigns[:doc_base],
        workspace,
        Map.get(addresses, version.id),
        assigns[:lang_param],
        version_query(version, latest, assigns[:version_param])
      )
  }
end)
|> Enum.filter(& &1.href)

helpers.name: language_links
helpers.code:
# A SWITCH OFFERS ONLY WHAT IT CAN SWITCH TO. `:lang` is a page capture and a capture only answers
# `site.languages`, so a document translated into French on a site publishing English and Persian
# has no URL here at all — `served?/2` is what knows that. A chip leading nowhere is worse than no
# chip in a control whose whole purpose is to be clicked, so those editions are dropped before the
# links are built, and a switch left offering only the edition already being read is dropped too.
# A chip ROW is the other way round: see `edition_links/4` on doc-workspace-list.
variants = Enum.filter(variants_of(workspace, assigns[:visitor]), &served?(assigns[:doc_base], &1))
newest = latest_versions_of(variants, assigns[:visitor])

addresses =
  newest
  |> Map.values()
  |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
  |> Enum.map(& &1.id)
  |> translated_slugs(page, assigns[:visitor])

Enum.map(variants, fn variant ->
  # THE CHIP FOR THE EDITION BEING READ LEADS BACK TO THIS PAGE. Built like the others it would
  # send a reader on ?v=0.9.0 to the latest version, and to whatever page that version files under
  # the lineage — from the one chip marked as the one they are already on.
  {address, extra} =
    case variant.id == workspace.id do
      true ->
        {page && page.address, version_query(version, latest, assigns[:version_param])}

      false ->
        mapped =
          case Map.get(newest, variant.id) do
            nil -> nil
            newest_version -> Map.get(addresses, newest_version.id)
          end

        {mapped, %{}}
    end

  %{
    workspace: variant,
    current: variant.id == workspace.id,
    href: landing_or_page(assigns[:doc_base], variant, address, assigns[:lang_param], extra)
  }
end)
|> Enum.filter(& &1.href)
|> case do
  [_the_only_one_left] -> []
  offered -> offered
end

helpers.code:
# A READ THAT DIED TAKES THE BLOCK'S OWN STATE WITH IT AND NOTHING ELSE. The task is unlinked
# before it re-raises — see `Phoenix.LiveView.Async.do_async/5` — so the page around this block is

helpers.code:
# THE SITE'S NAME, NOT ITS ID, because that is what a component is addressed by: the runtime hashes
# a module out of (component name, site name). Every `<.component …/>` below draws a sibling of this
# one, which lives on the same site as this one and nowhere else.

helpers.name: asked
helpers.code:
# THE LINK BUILDERS READ THEIR BASES OFF THIS TOO, which is why the addresses are part of the
# term and not just the URL keys: `version_links/6` and `language_links/5` are handed this map in
# the task, where the socket's assigns do not exist.
%{
  visitor: assigns[:current_user],
  workspace: asked_workspace(assigns),
  pinned: trimmed(assigns[:workspace]) != "",
  path: asked_path(assigns),
  language: asked_language(assigns),
  version: from_url(assigns, :version_param),
  section: from_url(assigns, :section_param),
  show: trimmed(assigns[:show]),
  show_banner: assigns[:show_banner] == true,
  doc_base: assigns[:doc_base],
  lang_param: assigns[:lang_param],
  version_param: assigns[:version_param]
}

helpers.name: fetch
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT FAILS ENDS HERE AS `{:error, _}`, which `arrived/2` draws as the block's error.
with {:ok, workspace} <- workspace_row(asked.workspace, asked.path, asked.language, asked.pinned),
     {:ok, versions} <- versions_of(workspace),
     version = pick_version(versions, asked.version),
     latest = latest_of(versions),
     older = version != nil and latest != nil and version.id != latest.id,
     banner? = older and asked.show_banner,
     # NOTHING IS READ FOR A SWITCH THE AUTHOR TURNED OFF. A header showing versions alone would
     # otherwise pay for the language side of it. The one read the banner needs is the version
     # switch's own, so a banner without a switch still costs one rather than sending the reader to
     # a page the latest version does not have.
     wants_versions? = workspace != nil and (asked.show in ["both", "version"] or banner?),
     # THE PAGES OF ALL THE VERSIONS THE SWITCH OFFERS, or of the one shown when it offers none, in
     # one read.
     {:ok, pages} <-
       version_pages((wants_versions? && versions) || List.wrap(version), asked.visitor) do
  page = page_at(version, asked.section, pages)
  addresses = (wants_versions? && lineage_slugs(page, pages)) || %{}

  {:ok,
   %{
     document: workspace,
     version: version,
     latest: latest,
     version_links:
       (workspace != nil and asked.show in ["both", "version"] and
          version_links(asked, workspace, versions, addresses, version, latest)) || [],
     variants:
       (workspace != nil and asked.show in ["both", "language"] and
          language_links(asked, workspace, page, version, latest)) || [],
     older: older,
     latest_href:
       (banner? &&
          landing_or_page(
            asked.doc_base,
            workspace,
            Map.get(addresses, latest.id),
            asked.lang_param,
            %{}
          )) || nil,
     language: (workspace && workspace.language) || asked.language
   }}
end

helpers.code:
Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
  loading: false,
  failed: false,
  document: data.document,
  version: data.version,
  latest: data.latest,
  version_links: data.version_links,

  older: data.older,
  latest_href: data.latest_href,

helpers.name: arrived
helpers.code:
Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
  loading: false,
  failed: true,
  version_links: [],
  variants: [],
  older: false,
  latest_href: nil
)

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.
socket.private[:runtime_cold] == true

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        # IN THE PAGE'S SITE AND LOCALE: `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4` hands the task both, so
        # `site_path/2` and `t/1` answer in it what they answer in the template.
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:switches, fn -> fetch(asked) end)
    end
end

helpers.name: doc_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF AN EDITION, built by `site_path/2` for the site the page renders for — in the
# template and in the task a block reads in alike, because `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4`
# hands the task the page's site. Each segment is appended to the base, and a `:lang` in the base —
# in any position, /:lang/docs or /docs/:lang — is filled with the language of the edition being
# linked to, not the one the page is read in, which is the only way a link to an edition in ANOTHER
# language can be built. The address is the one the site's URL mode gives that language:
# /docs/<document> in a first language the site leaves unprefixed, /fa/docs/<document> in Persian. A
# base without the segment carries the language as a query key instead, so nothing appends it twice.
# An edition whose language this site does not publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than
# a link to a 404.
numbered = Enum.with_index(segments)
pattern = Enum.reduce(numbered, to_string(base), fn {_segment, at}, acc -> acc <> "/:segment#{at}" end)

captures =
  numbered
  |> Map.new(fn {segment, at} -> {"segment#{at}", to_string(segment)} end)
  |> Map.put("lang", trimmed(language))

case site_path(pattern, captures) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    in_path? = ":lang" in String.split(to_string(base), "/")

    query =
      case {in_path?, trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
        {false, key, code} when key != "" and code != "" -> Map.put(extra, key, code)
        _carried_by_the_path_or_not_asked_for -> extra
      end

    case URI.encode_query(query) do
      "" -> path
      encoded -> path <> "?" <> encoded
    end
end

# THE ADDRESS OF A DOCUMENT, OR OF ONE OF ITS PAGES. A document with an Address of its own is read
# there and its pages under it — /product/docs/headless/switch — and that address is one edition's,
# so no `?lang=` is written onto it; any other is read under the base, by its slug.
case document do
  %{path: own} when is_binary(own) and own != "" ->
    doc_href(own, segments, document.language, "", extra)

  _read_by_its_slug ->
    doc_href(base, [document.slug | segments], document.language, lang_param, extra)
end

helpers.name: rooted?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER WALKING UP FROM A PAGE EVER REACHES THE TOP. A pair of pages filed under each other is
# reachable from neither end, and a tree built without asking would either drop both of them out of
# the contents or walk between them for ever. Twenty steps is deeper than any manual and cheap.
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _gone} ->
    true

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    false

  {%{parent_section_id: nil}, _at_the_top} ->
    true

  {%{parent_section_id: parent}, _keep_going} ->
    case Map.get(by_id, parent) do
      nil -> true
      found -> rooted?(by_id, found, depth + 1)
    end
end

helpers.name: effective_parent
helpers.code:
# THE PARENT A PAGE IS DRAWN UNDER, which is not always the parent it names. A parent still waiting
# on a review is not published, and hanging its children off it would drop them out of the contents
# altogether — so they surface at the top instead, and so does anything in a loop.
parent = section.parent_section_id

cond do
  is_nil(parent) -> nil
  not Map.has_key?(by_id, parent) -> nil
  not rooted?(by_id, section, 0) -> nil
  true -> parent
end

helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE'S OWN PART OF ITS ADDRESS — the slugs of the pages it is drawn under, then its own:
# headless/switch. The parents are the ones `effective_parent/2` draws it under, so a page's address
# is where the reader finds it in the contents. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent,
# so the same one under two parents is two addresses. The front page's is empty (`path_up/4`).
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})
Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, path_up(by_id, &1, [], 0)})

helpers.name: path_up
helpers.code:
case {section, depth} do
  {nil, _at_the_top} ->
    gathered

  {_deep, walked} when walked >= 20 ->
    gathered

  # A FRONT PAGE'S SLUG IS NO PART OF ANY ADDRESS. It is drawn at the document's own address, and the
  # pages filed under it sit directly under that.
  {%{front_page: true} = front, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, front)), gathered, depth + 1)

  # A GROUP WITH A PAGE OF ITS OWN IS READ AT ITS SLUG: the first step is the page being addressed,
  # and the group's own page is addressed by its slug.
  {%{group_heading: true, group_page: true} = group, 0} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), [group.slug | gathered], 1)

  # NOR A GROUP'S, above the page addressed: it is a heading, and the pages under it are addressed as
  # if it were not there.
  {%{group_heading: true} = group, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, group)), gathered, depth + 1)

  {page, _keep_going} ->
    path_up(by_id, Map.get(by_id, effective_parent(by_id, page)), [page.slug | gathered], depth + 1)
end

helpers.name: section_at_path
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE AN ADDRESS NAMES: the one whose own part of the address is exactly the one asked —
# headless/switch. A slug is unique among the pages under one parent, not in the document, so
# `switch` alone may be two pages. Nothing asked is the document's own address, which is the
# version's front page when it has one: the one page whose own part of the address is empty. A group
# is the page at an address only when it has a page of its own (`group_page`).
asked = String.split(trimmed(wanted), "/", trim: true)
paths = section_paths(sections)

Enum.find(
  sections,
  &((&1.group_heading != true or &1.group_page == true) and Map.get(paths, &1.id) == asked)
)

# its `{{doc.version}}` the version's `number` (`with_version/2`).
# Only the pages with no description of their own are read for their text.
require Ash.Query

ids = Enum.map(pages, & &1.id)

case {wanted == true, ids} do
  {false, _not_drawn} ->
    {:ok, %{}}

  {true, []} ->
    {:ok, %{}}

  {true, _some} ->
    read = fn found, fields ->
      MishkaDocument.Section
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
      |> Ash.Query.filter(id in ^found)
      |> Ash.Query.select([:id | fields])
      |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: false)

         untold = for({id, nil} <- described, do: id),
         {:ok, texts} <- (untold == [] && {:ok, []}) || read.(untold, [:content]) do

|> List.wrap()
|> Enum.find_value(fn
  %{"tag" => "meta", "attrs" => %{"name" => "description"}, "content" => text} -> plain(text)
  %{tag: "meta", attrs: %{"name" => "description"}, content: text} -> plain(text)
