helpers.code:
# THE START OF A PAGE'S TEXT, as words: a hundred and sixty characters at most.
text =
  html
  |> to_string()
  |> String.replace(~r/<[^>]*>/, " ")
  |> String.replace(~r/\[\[\/?(?:component|slot)[^\]]*\]\]/, " ")
  |> String.replace(" ", " ")
  |> String.replace("<", "<")
  |> String.replace(">", ">")
  |> String.replace(""", "\"")
  |> String.replace("'", "'")
  |> String.replace("&", "&")
  |> String.replace(~r/\s+/u, " ")
  |> String.trim()

cond do
  text == "" -> nil
  String.length(text) <= 160 -> text
  true -> String.slice(text, 0, 159) |> String.trim_trailing() |> Kernel.<>("…")
end

helpers.name: with_version
helpers.code:
# EVERY `{{doc.version}}` OF A PAGE'S TEXT — `{{ doc.version }}` too — IS `number`, the version the
# reader is reading, HTML-escaped: in its code blocks and in a marker's attributes as well, so an
# install line or a link to a release follows the version picked. `\{{doc.version}}` is drawn as
# `{{doc.version}}`. With no number, the text is handed back as it is. `doc-section`, `doc-toc` and
# `doc-section-cards` carry this word for word, and
# `MishkaDocumentWeb.Live.ExamplePreview.with_version/2` is the same rule.
case is_binary(html) and is_binary(number) and String.contains?(html, "{{") do
  false ->
    html

  true ->
    filled = number |> Phoenix.HTML.html_escape() |> Phoenix.HTML.safe_to_string()

    Regex.replace(~r/(\\?)\{\{\s*doc\.version\s*\}\}/u, html, fn whole, escape ->
      case escape do
        "" -> filled
        _escaped -> String.slice(whole, 1..-1//1)
      end
    end)
end

helpers.name: plain

# A WORD A PLUGIN HANDS OVER, AS TEXT: a string, a number or an atom. Anything else, and an empty
# string, is no word. The template escapes it.
case value do
  nil -> nil
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> (String.trim(binary) != "" && binary) || nil
  number when is_number(number) -> to_string(number)
  atom when is_atom(atom) -> Atom.to_string(atom)
  _not_a_word -> nil
end

# A TONE IS A WORD A STYLESHEET KEYS ON, as `data-tone`: lower-case letters, digits and `-`. Any
# other is `neutral`.
word = plain(tone) || "neutral"

case Regex.match?(~r/\A[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}\z/, word) do
  true -> word
  false -> "neutral"
end

helpers.name: badges_of
helpers.code:
# THE BADGES A PLUGIN PUTS ON A PAGE, asked on `document:page:extras` as `doc-section` asks it for
# the page itself, with `card: true`: a card is drawn from what the plugin holds, and a plugin
# answering it fetches nothing. Only the header's badges are drawn; an event that cannot run, and an
# answer of any other shape, adds none.
by_id = Map.new(sections, &{&1.id, &1})
paths = section_paths(sections)

asked = %{
  site_id: site_id(),
  document: %{slug: document.slug, path: document.path, language: document.language},
  version: version && version.version_number,
  page: %{
    slug: page.slug,
    title: page.title,
    path: Enum.join(Map.get(paths, page.id, [page.slug]), "/"),
    parents:
      Enum.map(
        parents_of(by_id, page, [], 0),
        &%{slug: &1.slug, title: &1.title, group: &1.group_heading == true}
      )
  },
  header: [],
  tabs: [],
  card: true
}

case MishkaInstaller.Event.Hook.call("document:page:extras", asked) do
  %{header: header} when is_list(header) ->
    Enum.flat_map(header, fn
      %{kind: :badges, items: items} when is_list(items) -> Enum.flat_map(items, &badge_given(&1))
      _not_badges -> []
    end)

  _not_an_answer ->
    []
end

helpers.args: asked, document, version, latest, sections, pages, summaries
helpers.code:
# EACH PAGE AS THE CARD DRAWS IT: its title, its address, its summary and its badges.
paths = section_paths(sections)
extra = version_query(version, latest, asked.version_param)

Enum.map(pages, fn page ->
  %{
    id: page.id,
    title: page.title,
    href:
      document_href(
        asked.doc_base,
        document,
        Map.get(paths, page.id, [page.slug]),
        asked.lang_param,
        extra
      ),
    description: Map.get(summaries, page.id),
    badges: (asked.show_badges && badges_of(document, version, sections, page)) || []
  }
end)

helpers.name: fetch
helpers.code:
# A READ THAT FAILS ENDS HERE AS `{:error, _}`, which `arrived/2` draws as the block's error. A
# block placed in no page, or in one the visitor may not read, lists nothing.
with {:ok, placed} <- placed_page(asked.placed_in, asked.visitor),
     {:ok, version} <- version_of(placed),
     {:ok, {document, latest}} <- document_of(version),
     {:ok, sections} <- sections_of(document && version, asked.visitor),
     pages = children_of(sections, parent_of(sections, placed, asked.parent)),
     {:ok, summaries} <-
       summaries_of(
         pages,
         asked.visitor,
         asked.show_description,
         version && version.version_number
       ) do
  case document do
    nil ->
      {:ok, %{document: nil, cards: []}}

    found ->
      {:ok,
       %{
         document: found,
         cards: cards_of(asked, found, version, latest, sections, pages, summaries)
       }}
  end
end

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.
socket.private[:runtime_cold] == true

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        # IN THE PAGE'S SITE AND LOCALE: `MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async/4` hands the task both, so
        # `site_path/2` answers in it what it answers in the template.
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:cards, fn -> fetch(asked) end)
    end
end
